articles.title: Microsoft partners with Razer, 8BitDo, and Backbone on Xbox 25th anniversary collection
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Microsoft introduced a limited-edition Xbox Series X in a translucent green shell earlier this year to celebrate the console's 25th anniversary. Now, Redmond is sharing a set of matching accessories for PC, mobile devices, and Xbox that further the celebration.
The Designed for Xbox 25th Anniversary Collection consists of a Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K mouse, a Razer BlackWidow V4 75% mechanical keyboard, and a set of Razer Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed earbuds – all decked out in translucent green.
There's also an 8BitDo Ultimate Charging Dock for Xbox controllers, translucent Backbone Pro mobile controllers in three "heritage" colorways that oddly enough don't include green, a Sling Bag from PowerA, and a GameSir X5 Lite mobile controller that is offered in Xbox green.
Most of the accessories appear to be limited edition versions of existing products, often with a slight price bump. For example, the Razer gear carries a $20 premium over their standard counterparts. All are from third-party brands, not Microsoft directly, and are available to pre-order from their respective manufacturer's websites.
Back in June, Microsoft announced a 25th anniversary edition of its Xbox Series X. The console is finished in a slick semi-transparent green with a glowing front logo, and a couple of other hidden surprises that Microsoft described as a thank you to the community. Functionally, it's the same as the existing Series X, complete with 1TB of storage. Pricing hasn't been revealed, but it's due out in November in time for the true anniversary date. Tom's Hardware believes it could cost upwards of $899, but we'll have to wait and see if that price point materializes.
Home game consoles as a category have seen significant price hikes as of late thanks in large part to the ongoing memory crisis. For many prospective gamers, buying a new console is simply no longer an option as they've been priced out of the market. With no end in sight for the RAM shortage, prices likely aren't going to correct themselves anytime soon.

articles.title: X sent Nitter a cease-and-desist. Then it went after the source code.
articles.text:
X sent Nitter a cease-and-desist. Then it went after the source code.
When Elon Musk’s X sent cease-and-desist letters demanding that Nitter — an open-source alternative front end for the social media platform — permanently shut down its instances and remove the project’s source code repository, it went after the code itself.
While Nitter.net was the project’s main public instance, other developers can run their own versions because the code is open source. So taking Nitter.net offline doesn’t really eliminate Nitter, because its code can be forked and used to run independent instances, including services such as XCancel. X’s demand for the repository goes further.
Open source meets platform control
Open source gives developers control over Nitter’s code, but not the platform it relies on. X still controls access to its service, and its latest move shows how that control can extend beyond just changing an API.
Open source gives developers control over Nitter’s code, but not the platform it relies on.
Nitter used to let people read public X posts without an account, but that stopped working in 2024 after X shut off the guest access the project relied on, taking Nitter.net offline. Nitter later found a way back by using real X accounts to access posts, according to the project’s GitHub repository.
That got Nitter back online, but it also meant relying on X accounts to keep it running. X controlled those accounts and could change the rules around them at any time. That doesn’t necessarily put someone who simply downloads or forks Nitter’s code in the same position, since doing so alone doesn’t mean they’ve agreed to X’s terms.
X’s cease-and-desist claims
Those changes are now at the center of X’s legal case. According to the cease-and-desist letter — first reported on by TechCrunch — X says Nitter violated its rules by scraping data and accessing accounts and session tokens, and accuses the project of “unlawful use and circumvention” of its API.
X’s lawyers also cited the Lanham Act and Section 33.02 of the Texas Penal Code, which deals with accessing computer systems without the owner’s “effective consent.” But breaking a platform’s rules doesn’t mean the law was broken, too.
Breaking a platform’s rules doesn’t mean the law was broken, too.
GitHub’s code removal standard
Under Section 1201 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, software can be targeted if it’s used to bypass technology that protects access to copyrighted material, even when the software doesn’t contain that material itself.
A claim that software bypasses a technical restriction isn’t enough on its own to get a repository removed from GitHub. For a Section 1201 complaint, the company must identify the copyrighted material being protected and explain how the code circumvents the technology controlling access to it, according to GitHub’s guidelines for submitting circumvention claims.
X reportedly says Nitter got around its API restrictions to access accounts and session tokens. The question is whether those restrictions were protecting copyrighted material in the way Section 1201 requires.
The YouTube-dl precedent
A similar issue arose in 2020, when GitHub removed the open-source YouTube-dl project following a Section 1201 complaint from the Recording Industry Association of America. GitHub later restored the repository and changed how it handles these complaints, adding technical and legal review before removing code when a circumvention claim isn’t clear.
For now, the repository remains on GitHub, archived and read-only. The code can still be viewed and forked, even though Nitter’s developer is no longer working on it.

articles.title: Meta acuerda pagar más de USD 16.000 millones para cerrar una demanda por el uso de sus redes sociales entre niños y adolescentes
articles.text:
Meta acordó pagar hasta USD 16.680 millones para cerrar una demanda de 29 estados que la acusaba de diseñar Facebook e Instagram para volver adictos a niños y adolescentes, engañar a los consumidores sobre la seguridad de sus plataformas y recopilar datos personales de menores sin autorización parental.
El pacto, revelado en documentos judiciales citados por Reuters, pone fin al juicio federal en California que se perfilaba como una de las pruebas más visibles contra una gran empresa de redes sociales por el daño atribuido a sus productos en usuarios jóvenes.
El acuerdo también obliga a la compañía a introducir cambios para adolescentes en todo Estados Unidos, entre ellos límites diarios de uso y bloqueos nocturnos. Según la documentación judicial, Meta aceptó esas medidas a escala nacional aunque negó haber actuado de manera indebida.
PUBLICIDAD
La causa federal reunía reclamos de 29 estados, entre ellos California, Colorado, Kentucky y Nueva Jersey, por presuntas violaciones de las leyes estatales de protección al consumidor.
Los estados también acusaban a Meta de infringir la Ley de Protección de la Privacidad Infantil en Línea al recopilar datos personales de usuarios que sabía que eran niños sin notificar ni obtener el consentimiento de sus padres. De acuerdo con la demanda, la compañía utilizaba esa información para entrenar modelos de aprendizaje automático e inteligencia artificial generativa.
En una presentación antes del juicio, la empresa había sostenido que las autoridades estatales buscaban hasta USD 1.4 billones en sanciones, aunque los demandantes habían sugerido al inicio del proceso que la cifra estaría más cerca de USD 200.000 millones.
PUBLICIDAD
El acuerdo impone límites de uso y restricciones nocturnas para adolescentes
Meta no solo pagará una suma multimillonaria, sino que además deberá modificar el funcionamiento de sus plataformas para usuarios adolescentes en todo el país. La firma aceptó interrumpir el desplazamiento infinito (scroll) e imponer límites diarios de dos horas en Instagram y Facebook.
Para reducir el uso compulsivo y las interrupciones del sueño, la empresa tecnológica también limitará el uso entre las 0 y las 6 y silenciará notificaciones entre las 22 y las 7.
El acuerdo también incluye herramientas reforzadas de verificación de edad y controles parentales. De acuerdo con el diario, la compañía deberá además restringir funciones que psicólogos vinculan con comparaciones sociales negativas, como los filtros de belleza y el recuento de “me gusta”.
PUBLICIDAD
Según The New York Times, el convenio prevé inicialmente un pago cercano a USD 12.000 millones, que podría aumentar hasta USD 17.100 millones si Snapchat, TikTok y YouTube también alcanzan acuerdos con los estados y aceptan sanciones económicas y cambios de producto.
Diferentes estados, escuelas y adolescentes presentaron miles de demandas contra estos gigantes tecnológicos, acusándolos de dirigirse a los usuarios jóvenes con funciones de producto tan adictivas como los cigarrillos o los casinos digitales, inspirándose en parte en una estrategia legal utilizada contra las grandes tabacaleras en la década de 1990.
El diario neoyorquino señaló que el pacto fue presentado ante la jueza federal Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers en Oakland, quien deberá aprobarlo.
El pacto llega en medio de miles de demandas por la salud mental juvenil
Este litigio formaba parte de una ola más amplia de demandas presentadas por estados, gobiernos locales, distritos escolares e individuos que sostienen que Meta y otras plataformas alimentaron una crisis nacional de salud mental juvenil. Los casos federales fueron concentrados en Oakland, mientras miles de expedientes adicionales siguen su curso en tribunales estatales.
PUBLICIDAD
Meta, Snap, Alphabet y ByteDance aún enfrentan miles de demandas en juzgados federales y estatales por acusaciones de haber incorporado a sabiendas funciones adictivas para niños y adolescentes.
En Los Ángeles, un juez supervisa miles de reclamos de personas que afirman haber sido perjudicadas, o haber visto perjudicados a sus familiares, por el diseño de estas plataformas.
El acuerdo llega después de varios reveses judiciales para Meta. En marzo, junto con YouTube perdieron su primer caso por lesiones personales, donde debieron pagar USD 6 millones como indemnización. Ese mismo mes un jurado le ordenó pagar USD 375 millones en una demanda presentada por Nuevo México tras concluir que había engañado a los consumidores sobre la seguridad de sus plataformas.
PUBLICIDAD
Sumado a esto, el pasado 6 de agosto, un juez penó a la compañía con otros USD 567 millones y ordenó medidas de protección juvenil.
Meta sostuvo durante todos los procesos judiciales que había trabajado intensamente para proteger a los menores en sus plataformas. La empresa también argumentó que no podía haber engañado a los consumidores sobre si sus servicios eran adictivos porque la “adicción a las redes sociales” no es una condición psiquiátrica reconocida.
En una misma sintonía, las desarrolladoras tecnológicas acusadas sostuvieron que sumaron funciones de seguridad para niños y que están protegidas por una ley, la Sección 230 de la Ley de Decencia en las Comunicaciones, que exime a las empresas de responsabilidad por lo que publican sus usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
Según CNBC, el acuerdo actual también contempla “medidas reforzadas de garantía de edad” para impedir que niños usen las aplicaciones y nuevas herramientas para padres y tutores.
El fiscal general de California Rob Bonta afirmó en un comunicado que el pacto hará que las redes sociales sean menos peligrosas para los menores y que Meta aceptó transformaciones amplias que, dijo, reducirán el riesgo de daño en cuestión de meses.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Glean unveils Tau desktop workspace, claims token-cost edge over Claude - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Glean unveils Tau desktop workspace, claims token-cost edge over Claude
Glean Technologies Inc. today unveiled Glean Tau, a desktop workspace that connects the company’s enterprise artificial intelligence to a user’s local files, applications and code.
The launch anchors a broad slate of product news at Glean:GO, the company’s conference this week in San Francisco. Packaged with it were benchmark numbers aimed at Anthropic PBC. Glean said its testing shows a 5.2-times token-cost advantage per query over Claude Cowork, Anthropic’s agentic work product, and that Glean is preferred 3.6 times as often.
Tau runs on an open-source harness and pairs Glean’s enterprise context with whatever sits on the machine. The pitch is less of what Glean calls botsitting, the time users spend hunting for the right files, feeding in background and steering a model through each step. Tau can plan multistep work, carry it out on a user’s behalf and check its own output.
Glean listed file organization, document analysis and spreadsheet building among the jobs it handles. Coding and engineering workflows are an early use case, though the company said it built Tau for employees across the business, with the platform’s existing governance and cost controls carried over.
Cost runs through the rest of the announcements. Keeping permission-aware company context available to a model, Glean argued, avoids spending tokens on repeated retrieval calls that rebuild that context at runtime. An expanded Glean Intelligence adds centralized usage visibility along with administrative controls over AI spending. Administrators get enhanced auto routing as well, letting them push work toward efficient, balanced or frontier models depending on the price-performance tradeoff they want.
Six other products and expansions came out of the conference. Glean Transform reads real activity signals to work out how work actually gets done, recommends which pieces AI should take on and measures the business impact. A proactive task management feature drafts follow-ups and prepares users for meetings before anyone asks, with email triage pulling company context into the queue and independent agents taking on longer-running work. Interactive dashboards are being expanded to blend structured data with tickets, conversations and documents, refreshing as the underlying information changes.
The remaining three cover collaboration, governance and security. Team chat brings several people into a shared thread or artifact with Glean. The company’s AI Gateway is being widened to support more entry points, enforce restricted-topic policies through Glean Protect and extend governed Model Context Protocol access to organizational skills and personal memory. Context-aware threat detection draws on the Enterprise Graph to separate legitimate agent activity from data harvesting, exfiltration or destructive action, including cases where each individual step looks permitted.
Emrecan Dogan, chief product officer at Glean, said models keep improving and are increasingly interchangeable, while understanding of a given enterprise is not. Glean was designed around that in 2019, he said, and company context grows more valuable as AI moves from answering questions to doing the work, “because it tells AI what matters, what should happen next and how to act within the realities of the business.”
Two customers appear in the announcement. Rhonda Baldwin, chief information officer at LaunchDarkly, credited the platform with letting her teams scale AI faster without giving up governance. David Lee, director of people and places enablement at LegalZoom.com Inc., said recreating the same depth of context on other platforms would take a huge number of tokens.
Availability splits three ways. Glean Intelligence, the AI usage controls and memory via MCP are generally available. Beta covers independent agents, the AI Gateway, auto routing, team chat and the dashboard refresh. Tau is not out yet, and neither are Glean Transform, threat detection, task management, email triage, a meeting coach or skills via MCP.
The company also launched a global partner network, spanning resellers, systems integrators, cloud providers and private equity firms across four regions.
Glean is venture capital-backed and last raised $150 million in a Series F round at a valuation of $7.2 billion in June 2025.

articles.title: Review do Oppo Reno 16 F: beleza e autonomia que custam caro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Review do Oppo Reno 16 F: beleza e autonomia que custam caro
Testamos o novo celular intermediário da Oppo com "cara" de iPhone e bateria duradoura; descubra se vale a pena comprar o Oppo Reno 16 F
Design elegante, bateria de 7.000 mAh, tela AMOLED e câmeras versáteis: esse é o Reno 16 F, celular intermediário da Oppo que chegou ao Brasil com preço de smartphone premium.
A gigante chinesa vende o aparelho por R$ 3.699 na data de publicação deste review. Mas será que compensa pagar isso tudo em um celular dessa categoria? Ou melhor comprar um topo de linha de outra marca?
Eu testei o Oppo Reno 16 F nos últimos 15 dias e conto abaixo todos os detalhes sobre o modelo.
O Tecnoblog é um veículo jornalístico independente que ajuda as pessoas a tomarem sua próxima decisão de compra desde 2005. Nossas análises não têm intenção publicitária, por isso ressaltam os pontos positivos e negativos de cada produto. Nenhuma empresa pagou, revisou ou teve acesso antecipado a este conteúdo.
O Reno 16 F foi cedido por empréstimo pela Oppo e será devolvido após os testes. Para mais informações, acesse a nossa Política Editorial.
Na caixa, sem grandes novidades: a Oppo manda o manual, a capinha transparente, chave para chip e um cabo USB-A para USB-C, além do celular.
A gente também recebeu um carregador de 80 W na versão internacional, mas quem comprar o aparelho no Brasil vai receber o adaptador no padrão brasileiro, segundo a marca.
O design é um ponto alto do Reno 16 F, lembrando bastante os iPhones da geração passada. Ele está disponível em duas cores: roxo e branco, sendo que a versão clara traz um detalhe em 3D na traseira, que muda de acordo com o ângulo de visão.
O Reno 16 F tem bordas arredondadas, estrutura toda em plástico no modelo roxo; a versão branca traz vidro na traseira.
Apesar da bateria de 7.000 mAh, ele é leve, pesando 196 gramas. Com a capinha de silicone que vem na caixa do produto, o peso passa a 226 gramas. Capinha essa que também protege o módulo com as lentes, evitando que o celular fique com as câmeras arranhando na mesa.
O Oppo Reno 16 F tem as seguintes dimensões:
Na lateral, há um botão para acessar ferramentas específicas do aparelho, além dos botões Liga/Desliga e de volume. Os alto-falantes ficam posicionados no topo e na seção inferior do aparelho, juntamente com a entrada para chip e cartão microSD.
O Reno 16 F tem certificação IP69K, garantindo que o celular possui vedação total contra poeira e máxima resistência a jatos de água de alta pressão e alta temperatura.
No teste prático, o smartphone continuou funcionando normalmente após ficar debaixo d’água. Ele também traz recursos via software para expulsar totalmente líquidos dos alto-falantes.
A Oppo trouxe um painel de qualidade para um celular intermediário. O aparelho tem tela AMOLED de 6,57 polegadas, com resolução Full HD+ e 120 Hz de taxa de atualização.
No geral, o conjunto oferece cores vivas em filmes e séries, boa nitidez e fluidez durante o uso de apps. O brilho máximo é de 1.400 nits, que não chega a comprometer durante o uso sob a luz do sol, mas no modo claro.
Ou seja, prefira usar o modo escuro apenas em ambientes de menor luminosidade. Do contrário, você pode ter dificuldades em enxergar algumas informações exibidas na tela.
O ponto negativo fica por conta da falta da tecnologia HDR10 na otimização de contraste, tecnologia disponível apenas na versão avançada do smartphone, o Reno 16.
Já a proteção fica por conta do Crystal Guard, vidro próprio da marca que substitui o Gorilla Glass usado nas gerações anteriores, e tem nível 5 de dureza na escala Mohs. A fabricante chinesa também já equipa o modelo com uma película protetora.
Além disso, a biometria é feita via reconhecimento facial ou impressão digital sob a tela. O recurso funcionou muito bem, até mesmo com os dedos molhados.
O sistema de som do Reno 16 F entrega o básico para o usuário, mantendo equilíbrio entre graves, médios e agudos, sem grande destaque positivo.
No entanto, se você estiver em um ambiente amplo ou com muito barulho, pode ser difícil assistir ou ouvir música, mesmo com o modo que diz aumentar o som para 300%, via software.
Sinceramente? Não senti evolução alguma no volume.
O conjunto de câmeras do celular aposta na versatilidade, trazendo três lentes na traseira e uma na parte frontal:
O destaque fica por conta da câmera principal e, especialmente, para a teleobjetiva de 50 MP.
O zoom óptico de 3,5x entrega fotografias muito boas, com ótimo nível de nitidez, preservação de texturas e ausência quase total de ruídos em aproximações. O pós-processamento atua de forma equilibrada, entregando cores vivas sem soar artificial.
A grande decepção do conjunto traseiro fica por conta da ultrawide de 8 MP. A câmera entrega um campo de visão generoso, mas sofre consideravelmente em cenários com luz solar direta incidindo na lente, reduzindo contraste, nitidez e detalhamentos.
Em ambientes de baixa luminosidade, o Modo Noturno se comporta bem e a presença da estabilização óptica (OIS) na traseira garante registros de qualidade e sem borrões causados por pequenos tremores de mão.
O aparelho ainda conta com um Modo de Alta Resolução e recursos integrados de estilo diretamente na câmera: como a função Pop Cam, que permite aplicar tons e filtros antes mesmo de tirar a foto.
O Modo Retrato, porém, poderia ser mais eficiente. O recorte ao redor do objeto ou pessoa em fundos complexos apresenta algumas falhas, exigindo condições de iluminação muito boas para entregar um desfoque natural.
Já a câmera frontal de 50 MP funciona melhor quando o ambiente está bem iluminado. O processamento da foto fica equilibrado, mantendo a nitidez e a textura real da pele sem exagerar nos filtros. Além disso, as cores ficam neutras, garantindo uma selfie bem detalhada e com visual natural.
Em fotos noturnas, há notável perda de naturalidade e nitidez devido ao pós-processamento que tenta compensar ausência de luz.
Em gravações de vídeo, o celular alcança a resolução máxima de 4K @ 30 fps. Na traseira, a estabilização óptica atua muito bem para conter a movimentação do usuário.
A marca também nos enviou o Oppo Bubble, esse acessório magnético com uma pequena tela AMOLED. Ele funciona como um visor externo, permitindo enquadrar selfies ou controlar o disparo à distância utilizando o conjunto principal traseiro.
No entanto, ele é vendido separadamente por R$ 899 no site oficial da marca: um valor alto por um acessório que funciona apenas como um espelho auxiliar para selfies com a câmera principal.
O Reno 16 F tem processador MediaTek Dimensity 7300 Energy, com foco em autonomia de bateria, além de 8 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento – com a possibilidade de expansão via microSD.
O desempenho é o principal ponto negativo do intermediário da Oppo. Foi possível notar alguns travamentos irritantes ao transitar entre alguns aplicativos, principalmente em multitarefa. Ao abrir Spotify, redes sociais e apps de banco, de uma vez, senti que o sistema demorou para responder a alguns comandos.
Também tive problemas ao editar um vídeo no CapCut, já que o celular deu umas engasgadas durante a visualização dos arquivos de vídeo.
Algo curioso que aconteceu de forma recorrente foi a tela piscando aleatoriamente, principalmente quando usava o celular para passar o feed das redes sociais.
Mas é bom abrir um parênteses aqui: eu não sei se o problema foi o modelo de teste que a Oppo nos enviou, ou se é algum problema crônico da linha.
Durante a reprodução de jogos, eu não tive problemas de desempenho em rodar Call of Duty e Genshin Impact com os gráficos entre baixo e médio, apesar de o aparelho esquentar bastante com o passar do tempo.
Já ao exigir o máximo da GPU, notei uma queda de FPS que atrapalha a experiência de jogo.
Nos testes feitos pelo Geekbench 6, o Oppo Reno 16 F teve pontuação inferior a celulares intermediários e topo de linha de três anos atrás:
|  | Oppo Reno 16 F | Galaxy A54 (intermediário, 2023) | Galaxy S23 (topo de linha, 2023) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-core | 979 | 973 | 1.874 | 
| Multi-core | 2.581 | 2.763 | 5.021 | 
| GPU | 2.356 | 3.021 | 8.697 | 
TB Responde 🎯
A pontuação em Single-Core mede o desempenho de apenas um núcleo do processador, sendo ideal para tarefas cotidianas e simples.
Já o Multi-Core avalia a capacidade total do processador usando todos os núcleos juntos. Ou seja, importante para tarefas pesadas, como edição de vídeo e renderização.
O Reno 16 F vem com Android 16, na interface chamada de ColorOS. Então, se você usa Samsung ou Motorola, vai conseguir se adaptar tranquilamente.
Esse é um ponto alto do aparelho, já que é simples, altamente personalizável e com animações interessantes.
Aliás, se você conhece o Dynamic Island do iPhone, saiba que o sistema tem um recurso similar ao desenvolvido pela Apple. Ele possibilita trocar de música, acompanhar apps de transporte e outros recursos do dia a dia pelo topo da tela.
No geral, é um ótimo sistema. Em alguns momentos ele sugere alguns aplicativos da loja própria da Oppo, mas sem sobrecarregar o celular com anúncios irritantes, como foi a experiência com o Huawei Nova 15 Max.
O ColorOS traz ainda todo o pacote de serviços do Google de forma nativa. Então, o celular usa o Google Wallet para pagar por aproximação, além de ser compatível com o Google Gemini e o Android Auto.
Ainda sobre os recursos de IA, a Oppo traz também uma ferramenta chamada “Mind Space”, que a marca vende como “Seu segundo cérebro”.
Você pode capturar informações da sua tela e receber sugestões do que fazer, como adicionar um evento ao calendário, anotar gastos em viagens, traduzir conteúdos e fazer transcrições de áudio, por exemplo.
A real é que eu não senti necessidade alguma de usar esses recursos durante meus testes, mas é uma ferramenta que pode ser útil para algumas pessoas.
O Reno 16 F traz ainda um botão extra, no qual você pode cadastrar uma função. Porém, só é possível escolher entre as opções oferecidas pelo celular.
De acordo com a Oppo, o modelo terá até seis anos de atualizações de segurança, mas a empresa não especificou quantos updates de versão do Android o modelo irá receber.
Outro foco da Oppo para o celular é a capacidade de bateria. O celular traz 7.000 mAh de capacidade sem comprometer sua espessura.
De acordo com os meus testes de uso contínuo, a autonomia foi de 14 horas e 53 minutos de reprodução de vídeos via streaming.
Para uso moderado, o celular foi capaz de ficar um dia e meio longe das tomadas, mesmo usando redes sociais, tirando fotos, gravando vídeos e usando aplicativos de produtividade.
A Oppo disponibiliza um carregador de 80W na caixa do aparelho, com tecnologia SUPERVOOC, que fornece carregamento rápido quando o celular está com pouca bateria.
Foi possível carregar 33% em apenas 14 minutos. Já para a carga completa, foi necessária 1 hora e 20 minutos.
O celular da Oppo traz todo o pacote essencial de conectividade: compatibilidade com chips nano SIM ou eSIM, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4 e conexão 5G. O NFC é compatível com pagamentos por aproximação no Brasil.
A marca traz ainda o chamado O+ Connect, útil para transferir informações entre o celular e outros dispositivos, incluindo iPhones e Macs.
Sinceramente? Não pelo preço de lançamento.
O Oppo Reno 16 F é um bom celular para o dia a dia do usuário comum, traz tela de boa qualidade, câmeras que vão além do básico e bateria duradoura, mas seu processador intermediário não lidou bem com multitarefa e apps pesados em meus testes.
Além disso, o preço praticado está bem acima de modelos mais interessantes da categoria, como o Galaxy A57, que já sai por menos de R$ 2 mil.
Por R$ 3.699, você consegue comprar celulares como o Galaxy S26, Motorola Edge 60 Pro e o Xiaomi 17T, modelos com CPU muito mais potente, mais memória RAM e que também trazem tela, câmeras e recursos avançados.
Por isso, vale a pena ficar de olho nos Achados do TB para encontrar esses e outros celulares premium pelo preço que a Oppo está cobrando por este intermediário; ou até mesmo o Reno 16 F em um preço mais aceitável.

articles.title: Dbrand drops Tank case for AirPods Pro 3
articles.text:
Toronto-based accessory maker Dbrand just launched a new version of its ultra-durable Tank case for the AirPods Pro 3.
Available now for US$29.95 (about C$41.56), the Tank case boasts a tactical design with lots of texture and grip. The AirPods charging case slides inside the Tank case and has such a snug fit that the company even included a removal tool to help get them back out if needed.
Dbrand highlights how it designed the case to allow access to the capacitive button on the case and wireless charging as well so as not to hamper the functionality.
It even comes with a lanyard!
It’s a pretty cool-looking case overall and will help keep your AirPods safe from most dangers, like drops and scratches. It won’t protect against a tank, though, despite the name. But we can’t have it all, unfortunately.

articles.title: Mad scientist makes LEDs in his backyard — semiconductor wizard who made his own RAM turns his attention to using bathroom eBay laser to etch sapphire wafers
articles.text:
Mad scientist makes LEDs in his backyard — semiconductor wizard who made his own RAM turns his attention to using bathroom eBay laser to etch sapphire wafers
It involves lasers!
The Dr. Semiconductor YouTube channel only has a few videos, but the man is quickly making a name for himself. He's built a semiconductor cleanroom in his backyard and made his own RAM cells there. Matthew Hartensveld (his real name) needs to figure out a way to package (cut and write) the RAM cells, so he figure he might as well use the opportunity to make some free-range, homemade LEDs while he was at it. This latest adventure is part of his open-source Semiconductor.DIY project.
The entire video is fascinating and information-dense, so we suggest you watch it to get the complete picture. Hartensveld started off with gallium nitride atop a sapphire wafer, that he proceeded to break into shards and clean with a solution including deionized water, acetone, and isopropyl. The primary goal was to etch the top layer of the material in order to define pattern contacts. Chlorine gas would be the obvious answer as that's what's used industrially, but it'd be more than a little hazardous in this setting.
The scientist turned his attention to a household item that makes every nerd happy: lasers. He ordered a powerful one from eBay, and moved it into his bathroom so his dog wouldn't look into it. Hartensveld quickly came across the problem that there was basically no information online about using said laser, and after a few attempts he managed to etch some scribbles on the wafer, and then actual patterns. After this, he test-drove the "LED" shard by smooshing some indium on it and using a 9 V battery, and lo and behold, there was blue light.
Doing so left a deposit of metallic gallium atop the pattern, so he came up with a solution to clean that up to leave the etched parts clearly exposed. Using a vacuum chamber with a two-stage pump that sucked out 99.999999% of the air out, he deposited a nickel/silver layer for the positive contact, then a titanium/silver for the N-contact and top metal, using argon plasma as the top gas. Even still, he later regretted not letting the chamber run for a while longer to draw out yet more air, to reduce residual gas.
At this point, Hartensveld had a fully working blue LED, though still in a wafer. That's right, blue, the color of LED that was a mystery for decades until a dedicated Japanese engineer figured it out. At any rate, the time came to package these LEDs, meaning cut them out of the wafer, and add physical connections. A table saw with very thin blades didn't really worked out, so in pure scientist fashion, Hartensveld turned once again to the laser, focusing it at a specific point to melt away the sapphire substrate. After an adjustment to make this a multi-passs process, he finally had a full cut.
The madlad still needed to add wire connectors, and after evaluating a few options, settled on indium bumps, the same method and material used in digital cameras. Last but not least, since he already had a blue LED on hand, he added a layer of cerium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (just bought off Alibaba) to add a yellow filter to end up with an ugly but functional white LED.

articles.title: How do we explain OpenAI's executive exodus? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI is the original frontier lab. Its latest publicly released model, GPT-5.6, is one of the most capable and efficient on the market. Its desktop app for agentic coding and workplace tasks has seen its user base grow by about 15 million subscribers in the last two months.
OpenAI has also already filed to go public. So why are all the executives heading out the door?
Since the turn of the year, more than a dozen executives have departed, including CEO Sam Altman’s top deputy, the chief operating officer, a chief revenue officer, its chief marketing officer, as well as several different team leads. Yesterday, news broke that Chris Malone, the company’s head of data centers, left the company last week after joining in March 2025.
Some of those departures were due to health issues, and others were due to reorganization that occurred as Altman sought to cut expensive “side projects” and focus on revenue-generating opportunities.
Still, Malone’s unexplained departure is striking, if only because OpenAI’s primary advantage over rivals like Anthropic or SpaceX is its investment in compute. OpenAI noted to TechCrunch that the departure follows a reorganization of the company’s infrastructure team, which is now led by vice president Sachin Katti, whereas Malone once reported directly to president Greg Brockman. It’s not surprising that a senior executive might leave a company if he suddenly finds himself several rungs further down the ladder.
The frontier lab declined to comment on broader changes at the company, but it seems apparent that Brockman is reasserting his leadership. As co-founder and president, he played important roles building OpenAI’s early infrastructure, but he was relieved of most management responsibilities in 2019, when Altman became CEO.
After that, Brockman played a disruptive role at the company, according to Karen Hao’s book “Empire of AI.” His contributions to individual projects like GPT-4 were undeniable, but he also seeded internal rivalries that helped kick off the “Blip” in 2023, when the company’s board briefly ousted Altman as CEO. Brockman would take a brief sabbatical in 2024 before returning to the company.
Today, the infrastructure and product teams report to him. “I like to say that everyone reports to Greg at the end of the day,” Thibault Sottiaux, who leads the company’s API and app offerings, told TechCrunch.
The specter of the company’s IPO hangs over everything. In June, OpenAI said it had filed going-public disclosures confidentially with the SEC. Tapping into public markets would be a boon for the capital-hungry frontier lab, but it also brings the prospect of disclosing its financials around the same time as rival Anthropic, which is also planning its public debut. Anthropic, however, is reportedly profitable, while OpenAI is reportedly seeing its losses grow along with its revenue. Now, OpenAI’s IPO isn’t expected until 2027; the average company that files confidentially for an IPO usually hits the trading floor within about five months; SpaceX did so in less than two.
Altman’s public comments about a bad past 12 months at the company and the internal reorganization jibes with a narrative that the company got over its skis with its IPO filing and is now reshaping the organization to make more money and carry less dead weight.
There’s a common cycle for some tech startups: Brilliant founders create the product, then bring in an experienced CEO to scale the company and prep it to go public. There was a sense of that dynamic when OpenAI brought in now-departed execs like Fidji Simo and Kevin Weil, who were veterans of multiple tech businesses — and now we’re seeing it again as Brockman’s influence grows. Before OpenAI, he was best known for building out Stripe’s business, and internally for championing the company’s go-to-market efforts.
With so much high-level turnover, OpenAI will need someone to fill the vacuum. The company will also need to trim its sails ahead of the IPO, boosting revenue and cutting costs wherever possible. For both problems, Brockman’s influence may be rising at the perfect time.

articles.title: Anthropic staff told to work from home due to risk of possible security strikes
articles.text:
Anthropic staff told to work from home due to risk of possible security strikes
Anthropic responds to potential of strike action from security staff
- Security contractors at Anthropic were reportedly preparing to strike, but there's been no evidence so far
- Physical security personnel are important as AI spend rises and worker threats emerge
- Anthropic employees were told to work from home as a precautionary measure
Anthropic has told workers in its San Francisco offices to work from home temporarily over personal security fears following reports that security guards responsible for protecting the facilities could go on strike.
The AI firm's security contractor, Allied Universal, recently warned that its security employees may strike, but ongoing mixed messaging left Anthropic taking the WFH measures as a precautionary move instead of a reaction to an actual walkout.
Per the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), which represents many of Allied Universal's workers, no strike authorisation vote had been called.
Anthropic warns of security worker strike impact
The union also claimed not to have threatened a strike on these particular days, leading Anthropic's reaction to come as a surprise to the union itself.
However, the concerns aren't totally unfounded, with an underlying labor dispute ongoing. SEIU has been engaged in contract negotiations with Allied Universal and other California security companies since around April 2026, seeking higher wages, better healthcare benefits and more comprehensive job training for the thousands of workers it represents.
Neither Allied Universal nor Anthropic have commented on the ongoings. Importantly, Anthropic itself doesn't play an integral part in the worker negotiations, being just the employer of a third-party security company.
As for the landscape more broadly, security spending has risen sharply in recent years as companies seek to protect more valuable equipment, in light of major AI investments. Anthropic, at the forefront of AI investments and with its leading model families, could well be one of the biggest spenders in this category.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Despite no evidence of a strike, Anthropic's decision to send workers home for two days would have minimized impacts virtually entirely, making it a smart precautionary move. Its workers are currently required to be in office around 25% of the time, per Business Insider.
Unwelcome news for Anthropic
The news comes as Anthropic could be on the cusp of becoming a publicly traded company. Current WSJ reporting points to the company boasting of potential revenue opportunities of more than $30 trillion, putting it ahead of SpaceX's $28.5 trillion estimate.
Anthropic is also said to be gunning for a valuation of around $2 trillion, per the WSJ, also above SpaceX's early valuation of $1.77 trillion. Secondary market trading has implied a slightly lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion.
While concerns over strikes are unlikely to have a major impact on the company's potential upcoming IPO, the fact that Anthropic is headquartered in San Francisco (at the heart of these ongoings) does make the temporary measure unwelcome at best.
The news also proves how the AI boom has created intertwined dependencies far deeper than data center hardware and software – physical security personnel also play a crucial role to the degree that instability poses potential risks to company offices.
And with both Anthropic and OpenAI workers recently facing threats, security remains a major focus.

articles.title: „Was, wenn ich Claude bitte, Krebs zu heilen?“: KI rüttelt an Patentvergabe für Medikamente
articles.text:
KI erfindet neues Medikament gegen Lungenfibrose: Warum das heftig am US-Patentrecht rüttelt
Als das Biotech-Unternehmen Insilico Medicine 2023 mithilfe seiner Computermodelle ein vielversprechendes Medikament gegen Lungenfibrose vorschlug, verkündete es in einer Pressemitteilung voller Begeisterung, das Molekül sei von seiner generativen Künstliche-Intelligenz-Plattform „entdeckt“ worden.
Insilico ist Vorreiter einer ganzen Reihe von Unternehmen, die KI einsetzen, um schnell Wirkstoffideen zu entwickeln. Dabei geht es vor allem um solche Rezepturen, auf die Menschen vielleicht nie gekommen wären – um so möglicherweise den Wettlauf um neue Heilmittel zu beschleunigen. Denn KI-Modelle sind mittlerweile in der Lage, atomare Strukturen für Medikamente fast so einfach zu generieren, wie ChatGPT eine Dankeskarte schreiben kann.
Patente für KI? Ausschließlich Menschen können Erfinder:innen sein
Als es jedoch darum ging, ein entscheidendes Patent zum Schutz dieser neuen chemischen Struktur anzumelden, erwähnte das Unternehmen die KI mit keinem Wort. Stattdessen nennt das Patent fünf Menschen, darunter CEO Alex Zhavoronkov, als „Erfinder“ des Medikaments.

articles.title: NVMe 2.4 Update Adds Post-Quantum Security, Power Controls - EE Times
articles.text:
As the non-volatile memory express (NVMe) protocol moves to an annual release cycle, the latest updates reflect the growing maturity of the ecosystem and the rapid pace of innovation driving its advancement, including AI.
NVMe 2.4 incorporates updates across security, sustainability, and management as well as specification clarifications. In a briefing with EE Times, Mike Allison, chair of the NVMe Errata Task Group, said the update bundles together a year of work across existing specifications rather than introducing entirely new ones. “We’ve been very busy,” Allison said.
Since the previous release, the non-profit NVM Express consortium has authorized 17 new technical proposals and completed 15 proposals, along with multiple engineering change notices. Allison said most of them were modified because the organization now has an errata group, which clarifies text when needed or when specification conflicts arise.
Due to the age of the storage protocol, some features are simply no longer being used, he added.
When NVMe 2.0 was released in 2021, it was “refactored” to break away the base specification from others that provide specific functionalities to allow for faster and simpler development in what has become an increasingly diverse device environment.
Securing NVMe for the post-quantum era
A major focus of this release is strengthening security, particularly for virtualized and cloud-based environments, as well as addressing the threat to encryption posed by quantum computing.
The update adds an information package for Trusted Execution Environment Device Interface Security Protocol (TDISP) that enables controllers to report detailed state information. Allison said the capability can be used to validate controller status when systems or workloads are migrated between servers. “You can validate what was the state when you left the controller in the source to what is the state in the destination when you’re continuing,” he said.
The specification also introduces improvements to lockdown functionality. Previously, lockdown settings were lost after a power cycle. The update now allows those settings to persist across reboots and introduces separate lockdown controls for virtualized environments, Allison said.
NVMe 2.4 also addresses emerging cybersecurity requirements through support for post-quantum cryptography (PQC). “We’ve updated our asymmetric cryptographic key exchange algorithms to be prepared for the PQC changes,” Allison said.
Sustainability features improve autonomous power management
The NVMe update also builds on earlier power-monitoring capabilities with the addition of voltage monitoring, which enables SSDs to identify discrepancies between the voltage supplied by the platform and the voltage actually received by the device. Allison said this feature can track measurements over time and across power cycles, helping organizations diagnose potential infrastructure issues.
While power efficiency remains important across all markets, Allison noted that client devices continue to drive much of the innovation. “Most of the power work coming in is for client devices and laptops,” he said, though enterprise and data center deployments ultimately benefit from the same advancements.
The release also introduces idle I/O exit latency limits that give hosts greater control over autonomous power management. Rather than allowing the SSD to optimize solely for power savings, hosts can specify latency thresholds that must be maintained.
Another addition enables restoration of a device to go back to the way it was when it was shipped so it can be reprogrammed from scratch. Allison said this simplifies deployment for OEMs that configure devices with multiple operational personalities.
Enhanced management subhead
The most substantial architectural developments in NVMe 2.4 include PCIe exported NVM subsystem migration and rate-limiting capabilities designed for shared PCIe environments.
The exported subsystem work enables the creation of virtual SSDs within physical SSDs, allowing virtual machines to access only designated controllers and namespaces, Allison said. “We’re moving the hardware abstraction from the hypervisor into the SSD itself.”
He said this allows virtual machines to communicate more directly with storage resources while maintaining migration flexibility.
The rate limiting feature adds new controls for allocating PCIe bandwidth and IOPS among multiple controllers sharing a transport. Allison said that NVMe previously had no ability to decide which controller got which portion of the PCIe bandwidth and IOPS.
Additional management improvements include host-addressable subsystem local memory, reclaim-unit scope reporting, NVMe-MI status reporting, and a redesigned NVMe-MI architecture that reduces redundant data structures and memory consumption. The release also adds support for the new SFF E2 form factor and improves management behavior in inter-integrated circuit (I2C) environments.
Looking ahead
NVMe technology continues to expand far beyond its origins as a PCIe SSD interface, becoming the common storage architecture across client devices, enterprise systems, cloud infrastructure, AI platforms, and even automotive applications. NVMe now spans nearly every major computing market. “It’s used everywhere,” Allison said. “Automotive is doing NVMe. Phones are, tablets are, laptops are. It’s really growing.”
But despite NVMe’s widespread adoption, Allison believes the technology is still accelerating rather than slowing down. “If I took the specs and printed them all out, we grew by 10%,” he said. “That 10% is bigger than the initial NVMe release. When I look at the last two releases, the rate of change is greater in the last two releases than in the history of NVMe.”
Beyond the current release, Allison said the NVMe community is already exploring future capabilities aimed at AI workloads, I/O prioritization, distributed namespaces, and new transport technologies. While AI is influencing development priorities, he emphasized that the focus remains on improving efficiency across diverse workloads and deployment models.

articles.title: ATF confirms “major incident” after recent Qilin breach claims
articles.text:
ATF, the regulatory agency that enforces federal laws governing firearms and explosives in the United States, has confirmed that one of its systems was compromised after breach claims made by the Qilin ransomware gang.
This follows Qilin adding the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives to its dark web data leak portal on Wednesday, without saying whether it had stolen files from ATF's systems or demanded a ransom.
The same day, the ATF published a press release saying that a standalone system was breached in what it described as a "major incident," which is now being investigated in collaboration with the Department of Justice.
"The impacted system operates separately from the ATF enterprise network, and there is no indication that the incident has affected the ATF enterprise network, the ATF eForms system, or any other ATF system," the federal law enforcement agency said.
"Upon discovery of the incident, ATF immediately terminated connections to the affected environment and initiated incident‑response and forensic activities. ATF is coordinating closely with the Department of Justice to investigate."
ATF added that the incident did not affect the agency's operations and asked the public to share any information on the attack via its official tipline.
BleepingComputer reached out to an ATF spokesperson with further questions about the incident, but a response was not immediately available.
Qilin is a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation first spotted in August 2022 under the "Agenda" name that has since claimed responsibility for more than 2,200 victims on its dark web leak site.
The list of victims includes many high-profile organizations such as automotive giants Nissan and Yangfeng, pathology services provider Synnovis, Japanese beer giant Asahi, publishing giant Lee Enterprises, and Australia's Court Services Victoria.
Several other U.S. federal agencies have disclosed cybersecurity incidents since the start of the year after their networks were infiltrated in cyberattacks.
For instance, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) confirmed in early March that it was investigating a breach affecting systems used to manage wiretap and surveillance warrants.
More recently, in July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security also disclosed a cyberattack that compromised the Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN), a sensitive information-sharing platform used by federal, state, local, and private-sector partners.

articles.title: Madrid ya sabe a qué sonará la Fórmula 1 en su nuevo circuito en septiembre: a un aluvión de quejas vecinales
articles.text:
El nuevo circuito de Fórmula 1 de Madrid ya calienta motores con sus pruebas para homologarlo. Para ello, los coches de Fórmula 3 ya han estado dando varias vueltas en este circuito urbano construido alrededor del recinto ferial del IFEMA. Lo que no ha sido tan emocionante ha sido la reacción de los vecinos que, si bien llevaban tiempo advirtiendo sobre el estruendoso ruido que podía ocasionar el circuito durante su puesta en marcha y construcción, ahora en las pruebas lo han vivido en sus propias carnes.
Y es que a varias semanas de que comience el Gran Premio de España de F1 en este circuito, varios vecinos afirman que el ruido era incluso peor de lo que esperaban.
Pruebas de homologación. Dos días de rodaje de F3 necesitaba el circuito para que la FIA pueda certificar la pista antes del Gran Premio del 11 al 13 de septiembre. Sin embargo, las pruebas se han convertido en un anticipo de lo que los vecinos temen que sea un problema mucho mayor cuando los monoplazas de F1 circulen por el Madring.
Cifras. Tal y como cuentan desde El Diario, la plataforma vecinal Stop Fórmula 1 Madrid instaló un sonómetro calibrado en la calle Francisco Umbral, cerca de la pista, y registró una media de 102,7 decibelios a las 10:52 h, con picos por encima de los 109 dB, según el colectivo.
El ABC recoge otra medición independiente por parte de un vecino de Las Cárcavas, a unos 450 metros del circuito, registrando unos 80 dB. Muy por encima de los 55 dB que, tal y como ha recordado la plataforma vecinal, es el límite legal durante el día en zonas residenciales.
Lo que describen los vecinos. Las quejas han llovido no solo de las calles colindantes a la pista, sino también de Hortaleza, Barajas, Alameda de Osuna y otros barrios situados a kilómetros de distancia, según Antonio Ibáñez, portavoz de Stop Fórmula 1 Madrid. Además, afirmaba que las personas que intentaban teletrabajar cerca del circuito consideraban que era "imposible" trabajar, incluso con las ventanas cerradas.
Constantino Bueno, otro portavoz de la plataforma y vecino de Hortaleza, cuenta que vivir cerca de Madring es ahora "incompatible con un barrio", obligando a los residentes a elegir entre quedarse en casa y soportar el ruido, o irse y acabar sufriendo el tráfico de vehículos que se genera alrededor del circuito.
Se avecina batalla judicial. El medio El Diario comparte las palabras del abogado Javier Flores, quien sostiene que “esto no es una anécdota de vecinos molestos. Es un problema jurídico serio,” señalando que la propia IFEMA había reconocido en un informe oficial que los niveles de ruido no se podrían mantener dentro de los límites legales durante el evento. El Ayuntamiento autorizó una suspensión temporal de los límites acústicos para el Gran Premio, lo cual es una práctica habitual en grandes eventos, pero Flores argumenta que esa exención “no elimina los derechos de los vecinos, ni les obliga a soportar cualquier nivel de ruido”.
Stop Fórmula 1 Madrid afirma que se está preparando con sensores homologados para recopilar datos durante el propio fin de semana del Gran Premio, los cuales prevé utilizar en demandas judiciales, además de las dos demandas ya existentes en los tribunales contra las licencias del circuito.
La defensa del Ayuntamiento. El delegado de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad de Madrid, Borja Carabante, ha defendido que las pruebas eran “imprescindibles”, ya que la FIA necesita datos reales para homologar la pista antes de la carrera. También argumenta que los coches de F3 son en realidad más ruidosos que los de Fórmula 1 que competirán en septiembre (bastante discutible esta afirmación).
Tanto los operadores del circuito como los responsables municipales sostienen que la instalación cuenta con las licencias correspondientes y está insonorizada acústicamente donde ha sido posible.

articles.title: Ce ventilateur mise sur le silence plutôt que sur les gadgets
articles.text:
| Ajustement hauteur | Oui | 
| Tilt / Pan auto | Oui / Oui | 
| Télécommande | Oui | 
| Batterie | Non | 
| Brumisateur intégré | Non | 
Le Duux Whisper 3 prend la forme d’un ventilateur sur pied assez classique, mais promet un usage tout en nuances grâce à ses 26 vitesses, son oscillation sur deux axes et son fonctionnement annoncé comme discret. Reste à voir si cette brise sage sait vraiment se faire apprécier au quotidien.
Avec le Whisper 3, Duux revient à une formule plus classique que celle de son Whisper Flex 2 Smart. Ici, pas de format table, pas de batterie ni de connexion à une application : le fabricant néerlandais propose un ventilateur sur pied pensé pour rester à poste dans une chambre, un bureau ou un salon.
Le Whisper 3 reprend les fondamentaux de la gamme, à savoir un design assez sobre, une tête circulaire, une base ronde et un panneau de commandes tactiles intégré au socle. Il propose 26 niveaux de vitesse, une oscillation horizontale et verticale, un mode nuit, un mode vent naturel et une minuterie. Le manuel rappelle aussi que ce modèle est destiné à un usage intérieur uniquement.
Le Whisper 3 fait donc moins dans la polyvalence connectée que le Whisper Flex 2 Smart, mais il conserve une fiche technique assez complète pour un ventilateur sur pied.
Le Whisper 3 demande un peu d'assemblage avant de souffler sa première brise. Il faut installer l'unité moteur sur la base, fixer la grille arrière, mettre en place l'hélice, puis verrouiller la grille avant avec une vis. Rien de très sorcier.
Une fois monté, le ventilateur inspire plutôt confiance. Le pied est stable, la base ne prend pas une place démesurée et le poids de 3,8 kg permet de le déplacer sans trop d'effort.
La poignée intégrée derrière la tête tombe assez naturellement sous la main. Ce n'est pas un modèle nomade à proprement parler, faute de batterie, mais il peut suivre l'utilisateur d'une pièce à l'autre sans imposer une séance de musculation.
Le réglage en hauteur est l'un de ses vrais atouts pratiques. Contrairement au Whisper Flex 2 Smart, qui obligeait à retirer ou remettre un tube d'extension pour changer de format, le Whisper 3 utilise un système plus direct : un bouton permet d'ajuster le pied entre environ 73 et 95 cm. C'est plus simple au quotidien.
Les commandes tactiles sont regroupées sur la base autour d'un affichage numérique bien lisible. On y retrouve l'allumage, le réglage de la vitesse, la minuterie, le mode nuit, le mode vent naturel, ainsi que les commandes d'oscillation horizontale et verticale. L'ensemble est clair, réactif et évite de multiplier les combinaisons de touches.
La télécommande reprend les principales commandes et permet de piloter le ventilateur sans se lever. Elle souffre toutefois d'un défaut déjà observé sur d'autres modèles Duux : il faut viser assez précisément la base pour que l'ordre soit bien pris en compte. On regrette aussi l'absence d'un rangement dédié sur le ventilateur. Un emplacement magnétique ou un petit logement aurait évité à cette télécommande de rejoindre les accessoires perdus entre deux coussins.
Côté modes, le Whisper 3 va à l'essentiel. Le mode nuit réduit la luminosité du panneau de commandes et coupe les signaux sonores, tandis que le mode vent naturel fait varier automatiquement la vitesse pour produire un flux moins linéaire. La minuterie peut être réglée jusqu'à 12 h avec un incrément assez large de 60 min.
L'entretien est celui d'un ventilateur à pales. Il faut retirer une vis, déverrouiller la grille avant, puis démonter l'hélice pour nettoyer correctement l'ensemble. Duux recommande un nettoyage tous les trois mois avec un chiffon doux légèrement humide et sans produit abrasif.
Le Whisper 3 ne cherche pas à rivaliser avec les circulateurs d'air les plus puissants du marché, mais ses performances sont correctes pour un ventilateur sur pied de ce format. À 1 m de distance, nous avons mesuré un flux de 2 m/s en vitesse normale et jusqu'à 2,9 m/s à pleine puissance. Le souffle est donc bien présent à proximité et suffit à améliorer rapidement la sensation de fraîcheur dans une chambre ou un bureau.
À 2 m, le flux reste encore confortable avec 1,4 m/s en vitesse normale et 2,1 m/s au maximum. La portée utile atteint 5,40 m pour un flux encore perceptible à 0,3 m/s. C'est un bon résultat pour un modèle de cette taille et cela permet au Whisper 3 d'être utilisé dans une pièce de vie sans devoir être collé à l'utilisateur.
Le flux reste toutefois assez concentré dans l'axe. À 1 m, nos mesures décalées montrent que l'air chute rapidement lorsqu'on sort de la zone directement visée par la tête du ventilateur. L'oscillation horizontale et verticale prend le relais pour distribuer l'air plus largement autour de la pièce.
Duux a baptisé ce ventilateur Whisper, et le nom n'est pas totalement usurpé. Le Whisper 3 sait rester discret, en particulier dans les vitesses basses et intermédiaires. Le fabricant annonce une plage sonore de 13 à 56 dB selon les réglages.
Lors de nos mesures, nous avons relevé 40 dB à vitesse moyenne. Le souffle devient audible, mais il reste contenu et ne gêne pas vraiment pour travailler, lire ou regarder une série. Le ventilateur sait se faire oublier tant que l'on ne cherche pas à exploiter toute sa puissance.
À pleine vitesse, le Whisper 3 monte à 49 dB. Le bruit est alors plus présent, mais il est moins agressif que sur certains modèles plus puissants.
La consommation est l'un des bons points du Whisper 3. À basse vitesse, nous avons mesuré 1,8 Wh sur une heure. À pleine puissance, le ventilateur monte à 16 Wh sur une heure. Ces valeurs restent très contenues, même pour un appareil que l'on peut laisser fonctionner plusieurs heures d'affilée.
Sur une simulation de 8 h d'utilisation par jour pendant quatre mois, cela représente environ 1,73 kWh à basse vitesse et 15,36 kWh à pleine puissance. Même en l'utilisant largement durant l'été, le Whisper 3 restera donc loin des consommations d'un climatiseur mobile. Il ne produira pas de froid, mais il ne produira pas non plus de mauvaise surprise sur la facture.
L'absence de batterie impose en revanche de rester près d'une prise. Le câble d'alimentation est donc à prendre en compte au moment de l'installation, surtout si l'on veut placer le ventilateur au centre d'une pièce.
Le Duux Whisper 3 est un ventilateur sur pied simple, agréable à utiliser et bien conçu pour un usage quotidien. Il ne cherche pas à multiplier les fonctions connectées ni à jouer les modèles hybrides, mais il va à l’essentiel avec sérieux : 26 vitesses, un réglage en hauteur pratique, une oscillation horizontale et verticale, des commandes lisibles et une consommation très contenue. Ses performances sont convaincantes pour son format et son niveau sonore reste maîtrisé. Le Whisper 3 coche les bonnes cases pour qui cherche un modèle discret, efficace et facile à vivre.
Le Dreo TurboPoly 765S conserve l’avantage pour ceux qui recherchent avant tout de la puissance, avec un souffle plus musclé et une capacité à brasser plus franchement l’air dans les grands volumes. Le SwitchBot Standing Circulator Fan peut de son côté séduire les amateurs de maison connectée grâce à son pilotage via application et ses fonctions intelligentes, là où le Whisper 3 reste volontairement plus classique.

articles.title: La SNCF va brader 200 000 billets OUIGO pendant seulement 2 jours
articles.text:
La rentrée est traditionnellement une période creuse pour les trajets en train : les vacances sont finies, les allers-retours des grands départs aussi. C’est justement le moment que choisit OUIGO, la marque low cost de la SNCF, pour remplir ses rames avec une vente flash. Une mécanique désormais bien rodée, que la SNCF applique aussi à ses TGV Inoui avec, régulièrement, des tarifs qui démarrent eux aussi à 19 €.
L’opération se tient sur le site Sncf-connect (ou OUIGO) du 2 au 3 septembre 2026 dès minuit. La compagnie y met en vente 200 000 billets plafonnés à 19 € maximum sur de nombreuses destinations. Le prix affiché reste donc le prix payé, sans supplément caché au moment de valider le panier. La vente flash ne dure que 48 heures, mais les billets achetés pourront servir à voyager entre le 8 septembre et le 12 décembre 2026 inclus. Une période suffisamment large pour couvrir les week-ends d’automne, les vacances de la Toussaint ou une escapade avant les fêtes de fin d’année.
Comment fonctionne la vente flash OUIGO de la rentrée ?
Bon à savoir pour organiser votre déplacement : une carte gratuite permet désormais de suivre en temps réel les trains qui circulent en France.
L’offre concerne aussi bien les OUIGO Grande Vitesse que les OUIGO Train Classique, avec des trajets en France et jusqu’à Bruxelles. Les départs du vendredi soir, les retours du dimanche et les trains placés autour des vacances scolaires risquent logiquement d’être les premiers dévalisés. Il sera donc plus efficace de comparer plusieurs horaires, voire les gares voisines, plutôt que de rechercher un seul train très précis.
OUIGO ne réduit pas uniformément le prix de tous ses trains pendant deux jours. La compagnie réserve un contingent de 200 000 billets à cette opération, répartis entre ses différentes lignes et dates de circulation. Une fois les places promotionnelles écoulées sur un train, les tarifs habituels reprennent le relais.
C’est pourquoi il est préférable de se connecter parmi les premiers, surtout pour réserver un vendredi soir, un retour le dimanche ou un trajet pendant les vacances de la Toussaint, prévues du 17 octobre au 2 novembre 2026. Le mercredi 11 novembre devrait également concentrer la demande : en posant le jeudi et le vendredi (ou le lundi et le mardi) il devient possible de s’offrir une coupure de cinq jours. En revanche, Noël n’entre pas dans l’opération, puisque les billets ne permettent de voyager que jusqu’au 12 décembre.
À ce prix, faut-il réserver son billet OUIGO maintenant ?
Un train à 19 € reste l’un des moyens les plus économiques de traverser la France, surtout sur les longues distances où l’essence ou l’avion coûtent bien plus cher. L’intérêt dépend toutefois de votre trajet : si la liaison que vous visez est concernée et qu’il reste des places sur votre créneau, l’affaire vaut clairement le coup.
À noter que l’offre OUIGO Essentiel comprend un bagage à main et un bagage cabine. Comptez 5 € pour un bagage supplémentaire, mais aussi pour un vélo plié ou démonté sous housse.

articles.title: Elon Musk veut la peau de Nitter, l'alternative gratuite à X
articles.text:
X a envoyé le 24 août une mise en demeure au projet open source Nitter, qui permettait de lire ses posts sans compte ni application. Nitter.net est hors ligne. Le développement du projet est suspendu.
Depuis le rachat de Twitter par Elon Musk en octobre 2022, puis son passage sous le nom X en juillet 2023, lire un post sans s'y connecter est devenu progressivement plus difficile, entre connexions imposées, quotas de lecture et API payantes. Nitter, un projet open source lancé en juin 2019 par un développeur pseudonyme (Zedeus), avait survécu à chaque resserrement technique en se réinventant. Proposer la même chose pour Twitter (puis X) relevait d'un tour de force technique. La mise en demeure du 24 août 2026 change de terrain : fatigué de jouer à Tom & Jerry, X passe par la voie juridique.
Sept ans de chat-et-souris
Nitter s'était construit autour d'un principe hérité du projet Invidious pour YouTube : récupérer les posts publics de X depuis le backend, retirer les publicités, les cookies de traçage et le JavaScript, et restituer le tout dans une interface épurée (sans algorithme, sans compte requis, environ quinze fois plus légère que le site officiel d'après les mesures du projet). Là où Invidious survit toujours pour les vidéos, Nitter vient de recevoir la mise en demeure qu'il avait jusqu'ici esquivée.
« Mise en demeure
Le 24 août 2026, la société X Corp. a envoyé des lettres de mise en demeure exigeant le retrait définitif des instances de Nitter et du dépôt du projet.
nitter.net est hors ligne et le développement est suspendu pour le moment. Je sollicite actuellement un avis juridique et ne ferai pour l’instant aucun autre commentaire sur les détails de cette affaire.
Merci à tous ceux qui ont utilisé, hébergé, packagé, fait des dons et contribué à Nitter au cours des sept dernières années.
— zedeus, 25 août 2026 »
Le projet ne passait pas par l'API officielle de Twitter, ce qui lui avait permis de contourner les premières vagues de restriction. La monétisation agressive de l'API à partir de 2023, qui avait mis à genoux de nombreux développeurs tiers, n'avait pas directement touché Nitter. En janvier 2024, Twitter a supprimé la navigation en mode invité non authentifié, rendant Nitter inutilisable du jour au lendemain. Zedeus a déclaré le projet mort. Puis il l'a repris en février 2025 en trouvant de nouveaux jetons d'authentification, et le service a fonctionné dix-huit mois supplémentaires.
La société X a envoyé les mises en demeure le 24 août 2026, avec un ultimatum fixé à 17h heure de l'Est le lendemain. Zedeus a confirmé à TechCrunch que d'autres instances avaient reçu des courriers similaires. Selon le courrier consulté par TechCrunch, X accuse Nitter d'un usage illégal et d'un contournement de son API et des données associées. Le courrier affirme que le projet aurait accédé à des comptes X et à des jetons de session, en violation du Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act et du Lanham Act. Nitter.net était hors ligne avant l'ultimatum, et XCancel, l'un des services alimentés par le projet, également.
La porte qui ne rouvre probablement pas
Ce que Nitter représentait concrètement, c'est un accès à des posts volontairement rendus publics, sans que X puisse identifier le visiteur ni l'inciter à créer un compte. Pour qui avait quitté la plateforme mais suivait encore des comptes institutionnels, des journalistes ou des services publics via des fils RSS, c'était la seule voie praticable depuis que X avait imposé connexion obligatoire et quotas de lecture à l'été 2023.
La mécanique juridique est plus difficile à contourner que la mécanique technique. Bloquer un accès invité, c'est une ligne de configuration ; répondre à une mise en demeure, c'est engager des frais que peu de projets bénévoles peuvent assumer. Zedeus a précisé chercher un conseil juridique mais ne pas pouvoir s'exprimer sur les détails pour l'instant.
La question de fond soulevée par des observateurs européens est celle de l'accès aux données publiques : peut-on restreindre l'accès à des posts volontairement publiés sur une très grande plateforme au sens du DSA ? X est soumis aux obligations du DSA depuis 2023, mais l'interopérabilité obligatoire relève davantage du DMA. Or la Commission européenne a décidé le 16 octobre 2024 de ne pas désigner le réseau social de X comme contrôleur d'accès, estimant qu'il ne constituait pas un point d'accès majeur entre les entreprises et leurs utilisateurs. La porte juridique est, elle aussi, probablement étroite.

articles.title: KollegeApply launches Orbit at Elevate Bengaluru to simplify AI-led student admissions
articles.text:
KollegeApply launches Orbit at Elevate Bengaluru to simplify AI-led student admissions
KollegeApply unveils Orbit, an AI-powered conversational assistant covering 10,000+ institutions and 200+ exams, helping students move from fragmented searches to informed decisions.
Choosing a college today often means navigating multiple websites, entrance examination portals, PDFs, forums, and fee pages before students can begin comparing their options. While information is readily available, finding, connecting, and understanding it can unnecessarily complicate one of the most important decisions in a student's life.
KollegeApply is addressing this challenge with Orbit, an AI-powered conversational admissions assistant unveiled at the Bengaluru chapter of Elevate on August 22, 2026. The second chapter of Elevate brought together leaders from the higher education ecosystem to discuss the future of admissions, institutional growth, innovation, technology, and student-centric strategies, with Orbit's unveiling forming a key highlight of the evening.
Orbit is designed to bring college and admission-related research into one conversation. Students can ask questions in their language ocabout colleges, entrance examinations, admissions, eligibility, rankings, courses, fees, scholarships, and placements - and continue with follow-up questions within the same conversation rather than starting a new search each time.
Orbit brings together information across 10,000+ institutions, 200+ entrance examinations, and 1,200+ courses, and is designed to be available 24x7. It uses KollegeApply’s broader AI-powered tools and decision-support capabilities to understand student questions, draw on relevant information and tools, and provide contextual answers across colleges, examinations, courses, fees, rankings, and admissions.
These capabilities include an AI College Predictor, AI Rank Predictor, Fees and Scholarships Guidance, Counselling Companion, Placement Insights, and Course Finder. Together, they allow Orbit to go beyond simply retrieving information and use KollegeApply’s AI capabilities to help students explore different aspects of their college and course decisions within one experience.
Orbit builds on KollegeApply's existing presence in the higher education ecosystem, with 60,000+ students having applied through the platform and 830+ institutions connected with it. This existing scale gives KollegeApply a strong foundation for understanding the questions, challenges, and decisions students face throughout the college admission journey.
Unlike traditional search experiences that return pages of results, Orbit is designed around the context of a student’s questions and the decision they are trying to make. A student can start by asking about a college, follow up about its courses or fees, and then explore admission requirements or placement information without restarting the interaction. The aim is to reduce this fragmentation and make higher education research easier to navigate and act upon.
Sanjay Meena, Founder, KollegeApply, said: “Our vision is to build an AI ecosystem where every query a student has about their college journey gets answered. From choosing the right college to landing the first job, we want a student to never have to look beyond one place for the right answer.”
Orbit forms a key part of KollegeApply's broader AI ecosystem. The company’s wider product vision brings together conversational assistance with predictive admission tools, rank prediction, college matching, ROI calculators, structured counselling reports, application assistance, and intelligent calling capabilities. The broader objective is to move students beyond information discovery towards informed decision-making by connecting guidance, prediction, and decision-support capabilities in one integrated experience.
The discussions at Elevate Bengaluru also highlighted the growing role of technology in responding to changing student expectations and reshaping the admissions experience. Against this backdrop, Orbit represents KollegeApply's approach to applying AI to one of the most important stages of the student journey: understanding options and making informed decisions.
For KollegeApply, Orbit is a step towards extending AI-led guidance beyond the admission decision itself. Future capabilities will include predictive college recommendations, predictive rankings, personalized college selection, and career discovery.
The longer-term ambition is to support students throughout their journey, from choosing the right college and navigating higher education to preparing for a career and eventually landing their first job.
The unveiling of Orbit at Elevate Bengaluru marks another step in KollegeApply's AI-first approach to higher education, with the company aiming to move students from simply finding information to understanding their options, evaluating opportunities, and making more confident academic and career decisions.
Orbit is now live on the KollegeApply platform.

articles.title: Hugging Face, pépite française, bientôt chez Nvidia ? Un deal à 12,9 milliards de dollars — Frandroid
articles.text:
Hugging Face bientôt chez Nvidia ? Le site américain The Information a révélé le 26 août que Nvidia aurait accepté de racheter Hugging Face pour 12,9 milliards de dollars, environ 11 milliards d’euros. Rien d’officiel pour l’instant : ni Nvidia ni Hugging Face n’ont confirmé, et les deux groupes, sollicités par la presse, n’ont pas donné suite dans l’immédiat.
Deux jours plus tôt, TechCrunch évoquait encore de simples discussions autour de 13 milliards de dollars (environ 11 milliards d’euros), sans accord signé. Rapporté au chiffre d’affaires, le prix atteindrait plus de 80 fois les revenus annuels de la plateforme, estimés à 150 millions de dollars (environ 128 millions d’euros).
L’IA générative crée du contenu en quelques secondes, mais souvent au prix de vos données personnelles. Avec Lumo AI, l’assistant européen de Proton, vos conversations restent 100 % confidentielles.
Mais c’est quoi Hugging Face ?
Hugging Face joue pour l’IA le rôle que GitHub joue pour le code : plus d’un million de modèles open source hébergés, et des millions de développeurs qui y déposent, testent et téléchargent des programmes. C’est aujourd’hui la plus grande plateforme de partage de modèles au monde. La société a été fondée en 2016 par trois Français, Clément Delangue (CEO), Julien Chaumond (directeur technique) et Thomas Wolf (directeur scientifique), et a installé son siège à New York. Sa dernière levée de fonds, en 2023, la valorisait 4,5 milliards de dollars (environ 3,9 milliards d’euros), et Nvidia figurait déjà parmi ses investisseurs : le prix évoqué aurait donc presque triplé en trois ans. Fin 2025, la plateforme avait pourtant refusé un investissement de 500 millions de dollars (environ 425 millions d’euros) de Nvidia, qui la valorisait 7 milliards de dollars (environ 6 milliards d’euros), pour éviter qu’un actionnaire unique ne pèse trop sur ses choix.
Nvidia ne se contenterait plus de vendre des puces
Après avoir écrasé le marché du matériel, Nvidia s’attaquerait à la couche logicielle et à la communauté. Posséder Hugging Face, ce serait contrôler l’endroit où les développeurs travaillent chaque jour, et les orienter un peu plus vers ses cartes graphiques. Le groupe avance déjà sur plusieurs fronts : il a récemment participé à un tour de table géant chez Perplexity, preuve qu’il veut peser sur les logiciels et les services, au-delà du seul silicium. Les grands laboratoires fermés prennent leurs distances avec le matériel Nvidia : OpenAI conçoit ses propres puces avec Broadcom, Anthropic développe la sienne et vient de passer une commande massive auprès d’AMD, Google aligne ses puces maison depuis des années. En perdant du terrain chez ces gros clients, Nvidia miserait sur l’open source, dont Hugging Face est le point d’entrée.
L’opération devra encore passer le filtre des autorités de la concurrence, et Nvidia sait ce que ça coûte. En février 2022, le groupe a dû renoncer au rachat du concepteur de puces ARM, pourtant valorisé 40 milliards de dollars, face à l’opposition de la FTC américaine et des régulateurs britannique et européen, inquiets de le voir renforcer sa position dominante. Racheter Hugging Face, la principale plateforme de modèles open source, placerait un maillon clé de l’écosystème IA sous le contrôle du numéro un des puces : de quoi attirer le même type d’examen.
Une pépite française qui passerait sous pavillon américain
Si l’opération se confirme, elle montre une nouvelle fois la difficulté de l’Europe à retenir ses talents de l’IA : fondée par trois Français, Hugging Face a grandi et s’est structurée aux États-Unis.
Pour ses utilisateurs, la vraie question porte désormais sur l’avenir de l’open source sous contrôle de Nvidia. Un groupe qui vit de la vente de cartes graphiques pourrait être tenté d’orienter la plateforme vers son propre matériel, voire de la refermer. Tant que Nvidia n’a pas publié de communiqué et que Clément Delangue n’a rien confirmé, l’affaire reste au stade de la rumeur.
