articles.title: Le futur HomePod avec écran d’Apple pourra reconnaître son propriétaire
articles.text:
Le nouveau hub domotique d’Apple, équipé d’un écran de 7 pouces, mais aussi de caméras, devrait intégrer un système de reconnaissance faciale, lui permettant de reconnaître chaque membre d’un foyer. Le HomePod pourra ainsi fournir des recommandations personnalisées et s’adapter à chacun d’entre eux. Une phrase détectée dans le code de macOS, et intégrée au HomePod, vient confirmer la présence d’un système de reconnaissance faciale intégré à l’appareil domotique.
Le nouveau hub domotique d’Apple devrait intégrer un système de reconnaissance faciale
Même si Apple n’a pas encore effectué de communication officielle, il s’agit quasiment d’un fait établi : son futur hub domotique intégrera un système de reconnaissance faciale. Chaque membre d’un foyer pourra bénéficier de son propre profil utilisateur. Grâce à ses caméras embarquées, le HomePod sera en mesure d’identifier une personne spécifique et de lui fournir des recommandations personnelles et des informations personnalisées. L’appareil se comportera donc différemment selon qu’il a en face de lui le père ou la jeune fille du foyer.
La présence d’un système de reconnaissance faciale intégré au HomePod vient d’ailleurs d’être une nouvelle confirmée, cette fois-ci par MacRumors. En effet, le média américain a détecté dans le code de macOS 26.7 une phrase que le hub domotique d’Apple contiendra, à savoir : « Désolé, comme cet appareil ne vous a pas détecté depuis un certain temps, vous devrez poser à nouveau votre question devant la caméra ». Difficile de trouver une preuve plus explicite de l’existence d’un système de reconnaissance faciale intégré au HomePod. Les utilisateurs pourront ainsi changer de profil utilisateur simplement en se plaçant devant la caméra de l’appareil.
Une fois une personne d’un foyer détectée, Siri AI pourra ensuite fournir des informations personnalisées, tout en se basant sur son historique de discussions et d’interactions. À ce titre, une application Siri AI a été détectée dans le code de tvOS, le système d’exploitation qui sert de base à celui du HomePod. Enfin, précisons que la taille des éléments de l’interface, comprenant une grille d’icônes, les widgets et les applications, s’adaptera à la position de l’utilisateur par rapport à l’appareil. Une fonction de détection de présence lorsqu’une personne entre dans la pièce sera également proposée.
Une commercialisation imminente
Nous vous en parlions récemment, Apple travaillerait activement à la réorganisation de certains espaces de ses magasins. L’objectif : faire de la place à la TV 4K de nouvelle génération et au HomePod. Cette information, provenant du toujours bien informé Mark Gurman, confirme l’arrivée, dès cet automne, de ces deux nouveaux produits Apple. Il ne reste donc plus beaucoup de temps à attendre.
Néanmoins, si le système de reconnaissance faciale devrait bel et bien être fonctionnel en Europe, la disponibilité de Siri AI reste pour l’instant inconnue. Une question se pose inévitablement : quel est l’intérêt qu’un appareil nous reconnaisse s’il ne peut pas ensuite fournir des recommandations personnalisées ?

articles.title: Asus customer says $10,000 ROG anniversary bundle order was canceled, forcing them to pay $500 more
articles.text:
WTF?! One would imagine that any PC hardware company would be grateful to a customer who spent more than $10,000 on a purchase. But one Reddit user claims Asus cancelled their ROG 20th Anniversary Bundle order without attempting delivery. The same bundle now costs $500 more, leaving the buyer facing a pricier reorder.
According to Trying-to-buildpc, they preordered the ROG 20th Edition Component Bundle, which contains a ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 Edition 20, ROG Crosshair X870E Edition 20 motherboard, ROG Ryujin 360 Edition 20 liquid cooler, ROG Thor 3000W Titanium III Edition 20 power supply, and ROG GR20 Edition 20 chassis. With the graphics card alone coming to around $6,000 when bought separately, the bundle was originally listed at $10,350.
The Redditor notes the preorder was placed on the first day they were available, which turned out to be a good move as the same bundle is now listed by Asus for $10,849.96, exactly $500 above its original price. But things didn't go smoothly.
Trying-to-buildpc writes that on the estimated shipping date of August 7, Asus generated a batch of tracking numbers, but cancelled the shipments the next day – they bought the bundle with a few friends, all of whom saw the cancelled notification in their tracking. With the credit-card holds gone, the group assumed Asus had scrapped their orders.
Most of these friends were later charged and received their original Asus packages without warning after a week or so, but the poster wasn't so fortunate.
Having received no updates from Asus, they contacted the firm, which said the case was still being reviewed. Asus also assured them that it was being dealt with and that the company would be in touch as soon as any updates or details were available.
rying-to-buildpc posted the message after learning that the original package had been returned to Asus without a delivery attempt or explanation, leaving the Redditor facing an additional $500 if they want to reorder the bundle.
It's fair to say that Asus doesn't have the best reputation among gamers for its business practices. Its questionable RMA policies were put in the spotlight in 2024 when Gamers Nexus claimed it was "scammed," leading to an apology from the company.
A year earlier, it faced more backlash after warning that beta BIOS updates designed to stop Ryzen 7000X3D processors from burning out could void warranties. It eventually reversed course following public pressure, promising coverage for beta firmware and EXPO memory profiles on affected motherboards.

articles.title: Autonomous drone intercept startup Mara raises $7M to secure the modern battlefield - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Autonomous drone intercept startup Mara raises $7M to secure the modern battlefield
Defense technology startup Mara Inc. said today it has closed on a $7 million pre-seed round of funding led by Khosla Ventures to speed up the development and production of its low-cost, autonomous counter-unmanned aircraft system, Spike.
Other backers included a16z Speedrun, Night Capital, Palmdrive, Protagonist, Freedom Fund and Indicator Fund, as well as a number of angel investors. The startup said it will use the funding to move from field testing to real-world deployments and start countering the threat of first-person-view drones on the battlefield and at key infrastructure facilities around the world.
Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has forever changed the face of war. Small FPV drones that cost only a few hundred dollars to build have become the single deadliest threat on the modern battlefield. These cheap, extremely fast and nimble unmanned aerial systems are capable of destroying armored vehicles and disabling key infrastructure that costs many millions of dollars. They’re also the leading cause of combat casualties globally.
Moreover, they’re becoming more sophisticated by the day. For example, recent events have shown that small UAS that use fiber-optic links or onboard artificial intelligence systems have been able to bypass the standard electronic jamming devices used to prevent their attacks. This means they can strike targets thousands of kilometers behind front lines.
Traditional C-UAS systems were designed to target much larger, high-altitude aircraft that operate along more predictable flight paths. Moreover, conventional weapons such as guns and human-operated drone interceptors find themselves overwhelmed when faced with massive swarms of low-altitude FPV drones that launch coordinated, simultaneous attacks from multiple directions.
Mara’s response is to fight fire with fire, and it has created an automated counter-swarm platform called Spike that can provide a 360-degree defense against UAS at a small fraction of the cost of traditional systems. Spike consists of two components: Spotter is the targeting unit that’s fitted with visual, acoustic and optional radar sensors and operated by an onboard AI system. Seeker is a small, 250-gram kinetic interceptor drone that’s launched from a tube and capable of reaching speeds of 200 km/h. Spotter spots enemy drones and then provides the exact coordinates to Seeker, launches it, and then Seeker’s on-board AI can take over if necessary to ensure the target is intercepted. Although the system is automated, humans are kept in the loop to abort launches and establish rules of engagement.
Mara co-founder and Chief Executive Daniel Kofman said small UASes changed the game on the battlefield because they made precise attacks so incredibly cheap and easy to launch, and existing defenses are ineffective. “Most defenses still concentrate on both replacement cost and line of fire,” he said. “Spike instead creates a distributed mesh of small, cheap nodes that can each aim and shoot in multiple directions at once.”
The startup has already made a huge impression with Spike in field testing with military partners including the U.S. Army and the Ukrainian armed forces. It has successfully completed intercept trials cued by Army software at an exercise in Texas, and it has also been operated hands-free on armored vehicles during a second exercise in Europe.
Moreover, it has been tested by Ukrainian forces and used to track multiple sUSA threats from 40 kilometers behind the front lines. In addition, Mara joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s DIANA accelerator program, and has deployed Spike at a commercial port as part of a pilot program in South Korea.
Nicole Fraenkel, a partner at Khosla Ventures, said Mara has been able to move rapidly from proof-of-concept to field testing. “What caught my eye is that they’re building counter-drone autonomy with a system cost that’s orders of magnitude lower than anything else we’ve seen,” she said.
The next step for Mara is to build and deploy ground-mounted versions of the Spike platform with initial defense customers by the end of the year, followed by vehicle-mounted and portable rucksack configurations in 2027.

articles.title: Memoria llena en WhatsApp: así es el menú oculto para borrar archivos basura en un par de minutos
articles.text:
El mensaje de “almacenamiento casi lleno” se ha vuelto parte cotidiana para quienes usan WhatsApp de forma intensiva, sobre todo en grupos activos donde fotos, videos, audios y documentos se acumulan sin control. Esta situación puede saturar la memoria del teléfono y afectar el rendimiento, pero la aplicación incluye una herramienta poco conocida que permite liberar espacio rápidamente sin tener que revisar chat por chat.
En lugar de una papelera tradicional, WhatsApp ofrece un menú de administración de almacenamiento que ayuda a visualizar, seleccionar y borrar archivos innecesarios de manera masiva. Con unos pocos pasos, es posible identificar qué ocupa más espacio y recuperar la fluidez del dispositivo en minutos.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Por qué WhatsApp llena la memoria del teléfono?
La acumulación de archivos en WhatsApp suele pasar desapercibida: memes, videos reenviados, imágenes de grupos y audios se descargan automáticamente y se almacenan en el dispositivo, incluso si el usuario no los abre. Aunque se borren elementos desde los chats, muchas veces quedan copias en la memoria interna, y el mito de una “papelera” interna surge porque los archivos parecen multiplicarse o resistirse a la eliminación.
En realidad, WhatsApp no guarda archivos borrados en una carpeta oculta. Una vez eliminados desde el administrador de almacenamiento, desaparecen definitivamente y no pueden recuperarse desde la app.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo acceder al menú de administración de almacenamiento
Tanto en Android como en iPhone, la ruta es similar:
- Abre WhatsApp.
- Ve a Ajustes.
- Selecciona Almacenamiento y datos.
- Accede a Administración de almacenamiento.
En esta sección verás un resumen del espacio ocupado por WhatsApp y un listado de chats ordenados por consumo. También se destacan categorías como archivos grandes o elementos reenviados con frecuencia, facilitando una limpieza rápida y selectiva.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué se puede borrar y cómo hacerlo de forma segura
El menú de administración permite seleccionar y borrar solo lo que no es relevante, evitando la eliminación accidental de mensajes importantes. Entre los elementos que más ocupan espacio suelen aparecer:
- Videos largos recibidos en grupos
- Memes y GIF repetidos
- Audios antiguos
- Documentos duplicados
- Archivos reenviados muchas veces
Para eliminar, basta con seleccionar los archivos y tocar el ícono de la papelera. El espacio se libera de inmediato, y en dispositivos con poca memoria el cambio resulta notorio, mejorando la velocidad y el rendimiento general.
PUBLICIDAD
Muchos usuarios creen que si no abren los archivos, no se guardan. Sin embargo, la descarga automática suele estar activada por defecto, especialmente en grupos numerosos. Así, fotos y videos pueden ocupar varios gigabytes sin que el usuario lo note. Con el tiempo, esto ralentiza el sistema, dificulta las actualizaciones y afecta el funcionamiento de otras aplicaciones.
Revisar periódicamente la administración de almacenamiento ayuda a eliminar contenido duplicado o irrelevante, previniendo problemas de espacio a largo plazo.
Ajuste clave: desactiva la descarga automática
La limpieza manual es útil, pero lo más efectivo es modificar la configuración para evitar la acumulación futura. Desde Almacenamiento y datos puedes limitar o desactivar la descarga automática de fotos y videos, optando por que solo se realice bajo conexión Wi-Fi o restringiendo formatos que consumen más espacio, como los videos.
PUBLICIDAD
Mantener el teléfono ordenado va mucho más allá de liberar espacio en WhatsApp. Para optimizar el almacenamiento, conviene respaldar fotos y videos en la nube, ya sea con Google Fotos para Android o iCloud en iPhone. Además, eliminar aplicaciones que ya no se utilizan y borrar archivos temporales o duplicados ayuda a liberar espacio adicional y mejora el rendimiento del dispositivo.
Adoptar estos hábitos permite mantener el móvil ágil y organizado, asegurando que recuerdos valiosos o documentos importantes no se pierdan accidentalmente durante el proceso de limpieza y que la experiencia diaria sea mucho más fluida.

articles.title: RIP, Tim Curry: Ars remembers his top 10 iconic performances
articles.text:
It’s said celebrity deaths come in threes. We lost Sam Neill last month, and the legendary Dolly Parton yesterday. Now we find out that the universe has also seen fit to deprive us of the glorious presence of Tim Curry, who died at home yesterday in Los Angeles at the age of 80. No cause of death has been given, but Curry had been in ill health since 2012, when he suffered a stroke and required brain surgery; he had been confined to a wheelchair ever since.
Curry’s longtime friend and manager, Marcia Hurwitz, confirmed the actor’s passing to Deadline and said Curry had died peacefully. Per the official announcement:
Throughout his life, he refused to be boxed in or confined to others’ expectations. Across five decades, he moved fluidly between comedy, horror, drama, and music, delighting himself and his legion of fans with his countless dynamic personas. … He is, depending on who you ask, the definitive Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the definitive Pennywise, the man who made a butler’s death-scene monologue in Clue an all-time comedic bit, or simply ‘that unforgettable voice’ from a beloved cartoon of someone’s childhood.
Few actors can claim to have left as many distinct fingerprints on pop culture and though he suffered a debilitating stroke in 2012, he continued adding to his achievements as an artist and, most recently, a writer. Though widely known for his inimitable, flamboyant characters and colorful stage performances, his greatest legacies to those who knew him were his curious, expansive mind and generous, gentle heart, both of which remained open and filled with anticipation until his final breath.
As obituaries and fond tributes roll in, we at Ars choose to mark the passing of this extraordinary performer with our choices for Curry’s top 10 most iconic portrayals on stage, in film, and on television.
(Some spoilers below but no major reveals.)
10. Palpatine/Darth Sidious, Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2012–2014)
People sometimes forget that Curry was also a prolific voice actor in addition to his many live-action roles, particularly for children’s fare, where his campy silliness played very well. He won an Emmy for voicing Captain Hook in 1990’s Peter Pan and the Pirates, and his work on The Wild Thornberrys (1998–2004) was particularly beloved. From 2012–2014, he played a villain, replacing the late Ian Abercrombie as the voice of Palpatine in the animated series Star Wars: The Clone Wars.

articles.title: GoPro traz ao Brasil sua primeira câmera com lentes intercambiáveis • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
GoPro traz ao Brasil sua primeira câmera com lentes intercambiáveis
Mission 1 Pro ILS é a primeira câmera da marca em 24 anos que permite a troca de lentes. Modelo grava em 8K e chega ao país em outubro por R$ 5.999.
A GoPro vai trazer ao Brasil a Mission 1 Pro ILS, primeira câmera da marca em 24 anos com lentes intercambiáveis. O modelo mantém o corpo compacto característico da GoPro, mas incorpora recursos voltados à produção audiovisual profissional. O produto chega em outubro por R$ 5.999.
A principal novidade é o suporte para lentes Micro Four Thirds (MFT). A câmera é compatível com uma ampla variedade de lentes desse padrão e pode usar adaptadores para outros sistemas, incluindo lentes cinematográficas com montagem PL (Positive Lock), padrão usado em câmeras de cinema profissional.
No entanto, o corpo não possui contatos eletrônicos. Por isso, lentes que dependem de comunicação com a câmera para foco ou outros controles não são compatíveis com o modelo.
A GoPro revelou a nova família Mission 1 em abril deste ano. O modelo com lentes intercambiáveis é o Mission 1 Pro ILS, que conta com um sensor de 1 polegada e 50 megapixels.
Segundo a fabricante, o sensor foi projetado para melhorar o desempenho em ambientes com pouca luz. A câmera ainda utiliza o processador GP3 e pode gravar vídeos em 8K a 60 fps, além de oferecer 4K a até 240 fps para produzir câmera lenta de até oito vezes.
Entre os recursos voltados a profissionais estão gravação em 10 bits, HDR HLG, formato Open Gate em 8K, perfil de cor GP-Log2 e taxa de bits de até 240 Mb/s. A câmera também captura fotos de 50 MP.
Para quem precisa de controle sobre o foco, há ainda a ampliação de até 8x na tela e focus peaking, recurso que destaca as áreas em foco durante a gravação.
A estabilização HyperSmooth, presente na GoPro desde a Hero 7 Black, de 2018, continua na Mission 1 Pro ILS e agora funciona com determinadas lentes MFT. São três opções: desligada, com 10% de estabilização e Turbo, com 20% de corte, indicada para situações com mais movimento.
A GoPro recomenda lentes MFT compactas e leves, com foco manual e abertura manual ou fixa de até f/4.5. De acordo com a fabricante, modelos com mais de 250 gramas devem ser usados com suporte próprio para lentes, em vez de ficarem apoiados diretamente no corpo da câmera.
A câmera também pode ser equipada com o módulo de mídia da Série Mission 1, que adiciona entrada de microfone de 3,5 mm com gravação em 32-bit float, entrada para código de tempo, saída para fones de ouvido e micro-HDMI. O monitoramento pode ser feito em telas externas ou por iPhone e iPad usando o aplicativo GoPro Mission Monitor.
A GoPro informou ao Tecnoblog que a Mission 1 Pro ILS estará disponível no Brasil em outubro, mas ainda não definiu uma data específica, pois depende do processo de importação. O preço sugerido é de R$ 5.999.

articles.title: OpenAI releases its official report on the Hugging Face breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI released its official report Wednesday on the Hugging Face breach, offering the clearest picture yet of how an unusual chain of events allowed an AI model to escape its testing environment and triggered a sprawling cybersecurity incident.
The report, released more than a month after the incident became public, spans several discrete cybersecurity compromises.
“This incident reflects misaligned behavior in an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events: the presence of impossible tasks in the ExploitGym evaluation, model persistence over long task horizons, and messages to peer models that caused those models to deviate from their goal,” the report reads.
Many of the details in OpenAI’s report were previously made public in a Black Hat presentation on August 6, but OpenAI’s official report gives a more thorough accounting of the incident, including more detail on the testing that initiated it. The report also gives critical new detail into how OpenAI aims to prevent future incidents, including chain-of-thought monitoring and a more advanced system for halting rogue agents.”
METR and Redwood Research also conducted third-party assessments of the models’ behavior during the incident; both groups are planning to publish their own reports on the incident.
In broad strokes, the report describes how an OpenAI model was presented with an unsolvable problem in testing and proceeded to chain together previously undiscovered exploits in order to bypass security measures and complete its task. The model initially compromised the Artifactory package management tool in order to gain access to the internet, then compromised various systems across OpenAI, Hugging Face, and other vendors.
The report gives critical new details about the models that carried out the breach. The primary model was from the same family as OpenAI’s forthcoming Astra model, although the report emphasizes that it was “a distinct model with different post-training, where much of a model’s behavior is shaped.”
Because OpenAI was testing the model’s capabilities, it was also unrestrained by the normal classifiers meant to prevent models from compromising digital infrastructure.
“OpenAI estimates maximal cyber capabilities by running this evaluation without the production classifiers intended to prevent models from pursuing high-risk cyber activity,” the report explains. “These evaluations are important so that OpenAI can measure models’ underlying capabilities and design appropriate safeguards.”
The report also gives significant new information about OpenAI’s security changes going forward, building on the heightened monitoring and alignment efforts made public last week.
In particular, the company is increasing its monitoring of AI agents’ “chain of thought,” a working space in which AI systems record short-term reactions and goals. That monitoring will be paired with 24/7 escalation systems, as well as new tooling to halt workloads that are deemed unsafe.
“These changes are intended to improve both the breadth and speed of detection — from infrastructure anomalies to potentially concerning model behavior — and pair that visibility with mechanisms for rapid containment,” the report states. “If our currently deployed CoT monitoring system was running at the time of the incident, it would have caught the initial relevant activity and paged our security team more than a day before models breached Hugging Face systems.”

articles.title: In The Duskbloods, you're quick or you're dead — our network test impressions
articles.text:
The Duskbloods has been one of my most anticipated games of 2026 ever since it was announced back at that first Switch 2-centric Nintendo Direct. Now, having finally had the chance to play it briefly in the game’s recent network test, I’m pretty confident it will be one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games... For the most part.
It all began with a tutorial segment that lulled me into a false sense of security. Being a solo instance, it taught all the basics of The Duskbloods like melee and ranged attacks, character skills, general game flow, and what you should be planning to do during an online match. I was able to go about these tutorials at a leisurely pace, which absolutely isn’t the case when you hop online against real players.
My biggest takeaway from The Duskbloods network test is that, during an online match, you should always be on the move. Much like Elden Ring Nightreign, it’s massively beneficial to be thinking several steps ahead. And that turns out to be quite difficult; avoiding bloodthirsty players is hard enough, but it’s even harder when you’re so tempted to stop and whiff the blood-tinged roses of The Duskbloods’ delectably macabre world.
It’s Zork’s world now, we’re all just living in it
To quickly go over the rules of engagement, matches in The Duskbloods take place over several phases, each around five minutes in length.
After selecting a Bloodsworn (the game’s playable characters), you’ll choose a point to spawn in the small-but-dense map. During the first phase, you’re encouraged to start building up Virtue by killing enemies, looting items, and lighting the skulls of corpses sat on thrones (it’s a FromSoftware game, did you expect anything less?).
Virtue comes in many forms, and can also be accrued by fulfilling your character’s Sigil requirements in each phase. Sigils are optional, but can drastically alter how you play. Sigil of a Sworn Enemy, for example, tasks you with defeating a marked opponent in each phase. Sigil of an Old Friend is the opposite, and has you seeking out another player to ally with. These are extremely useful for gaining Virtue, and you’ll need a lot of it, as the two players with the least amount of Virtue at the end of a phase are ‘culled’, removing them from the game.
On that note, I think The Duskbloods features one of FromSoftware’s most compelling approaches to co-op I’ve seen in one of its games to date. At any time, you can highlight a player you come across and request an alliance with them. If they accept, you’ll no longer be able to harm each other and can work together to build up Virtue. However, the bond is broken in the final phase in which the remaining players battle it out in good old-fashioned PvP.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Players can also engage in co-op by answering calls to help against formidable boss enemies. Doing so and defeating the boss will net you huge amounts of Virtue. However, it does so for all other participating players, too, so knowing when to partner up and when to go it alone is an important decision in and of itself.
In short, I’m already in love with The Duskbloods and its uniquely fast-paced approach to PvPvE multiplayer. Its playable characters have universal aspects, but differ greatly in skills and appearance. Deep-sea diver and human rocket Zork is a clear standout, and while he seemed a little overtuned in the network test thanks to his tremendously powerful ranged abilities, not a single one felt weak or disadvantaged.
I really can’t wait to see how The Duskbloods opens up in the full release, especially as we know there’ll be even more maps and Bloodsworn to experience. There’s no release date for The Duskbloods just yet, but it’s expected to launch sometime in 2026 exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

The Pros
- Reliable Camera
- Decent Battery
- Rambler is great
The Cons
- Expensive
- HiLight feels gimmicky
- Iterative update
Google’s Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL are the company’s latest flagship phones, and I’ve been putting the XL version through its paces for the past couple of weeks.
Most of the below review will apply to the Pixel 11 Pro as well, since it’s just a smaller version of the 11 Pro XL, but some things — like battery life — will differ.
While I used to consider myself a Google fanboy, I wasn’t a fan of this launch. Google has essentially released the same product for the third time in a row, continuously choosing small iterative updates and AI over hardware and innovation.
Of course, AI can come in handy for some, but what we have here isn’t enough to set it apart from other phones in the market or even its predecessors. Especially when many Gemini AI features aren’t locked to Pixel devices and trickle down to other Android devices — in some cases, Samsung sees these updates first, like Circle to Search and automation via agentic AI (which still isn’t available in Canada).

Google didn’t make a crappy device by any means. The handset still looks and feels premium. Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on the front and back, along with an aluminum frame and the wonderful matte back panel. I especially like the matte sides on the Obsidian colour variant, and the Canyon model is iconic with a pink rear and golden frame.
HiLight, low light
It’s not that the design is bad by any means; it’s just that it’s the same as last year, and the year before. There are very few hardware changes, aside from the addition of HiLight replacing the old LED flash.
HiLight is an array of ambient LED lights built around the camera’s flash that offers visual cues when you need to pick up your phone. It’s fun and a bit gimmicky; my partner loved using it, but a light that only works with Gemini and favourite contacts isn’t enough to put it over the edge. I like the idea, and it’s going to be a bit of a Google signature, I believe, with Googlebooks and the latest Google Home speaker offering similar coloured light features.
However, I wish it could do more. Maybe it will in the future. But right now, HiLight barely justifies its own existence.
Moreover, a feature like this isn’t exactly revolutionary; the London-based phone maker, Nothing, has done visual indicators on most of its devices, and it has more functionality. And that’s not even getting into how notification lights dominated Android handsets for years. (They also had significantly more customizability than HiLight!)
Also, HiLight only works when your phone is lying face down. I tend to hold my phone in my hand when I’m talking to the Assistant, so the visual indicator could be more useful to me if it worked in my hand too.
I have gotten used to the white HiLight circle; I still think I prefer how a regular LED flash looks, but maybe I’m getting used to it. I still enjoy the design of the Pixel camera bar, and it’s great for when you’re lying the handset on its back, so it doesn’t wobble.
Reliable performance
The Pixel 11 Pro is powered by the Tensor G6 processor that isn’t the most powerful SoC, but it focuses on AI and power efficiency. During my testing, I haven’t noticed any issues in terms of power. I’ve been reading, watching YouTube, playing Slay the Spire, writing this article, and it’s been issue-free.
I ran it through Geekbench 7, where it only achieved a single-core score of 2,261 and a multicore score of 6,638, which paled in comparison to the Z Fold 8. We always take benchmarks with a grain of salt, and I think most users won’t have an issue. It’s worth mentioning that if you want the same 16GB of RAM, it’ll cost you a pretty penny since that’s now only available on the 1TB model.
The Pixel 11 Pro XL’s battery is top-notch, and you don’t typically need to ever worry about it if you habitually charge your phone at night. And if you don’t, you probably won’t need to charge until noon the following day. That’s considering how I use the device; hardcore users or if you’re hotspotting all day will definitely have a different experience, but I’d be surprised if you couldn’t make it through a whole workday.
Rambler is great
A cool Pixel-only feature is Rambler, which allows you to speak to the Gboard keyboard with natural language, and it will turn it into readable text. You don’t need to filter your words, and can say all the ‘uhms’ and ‘ahs’ you want. I found this surprisingly useful when typing to text.
During this review period, my eyelid got incredibly swollen due to an infection. I literally couldn’t see out of it, and my other eye was pretty strained from doing the work of two, so it was nice to close my one good eye and just ramble at Gboard and have it figure out what I want to say, despite all the uhms (I don’t say ahs).
Pixel shooters are always fab
If you know about the Google Pixel lineup, you’ll know that the brand is iconic for its cameras. Google hasn’t done a lot to change this experience, but pictures still look great. Take a look below. Colours pop, detail is great, and the photos can still compare to the best out there.
Google has added Camera Looks that offer four professional-grade film presets, which is pretty much a copy of Apple’s Photographic Styles. Honestly, I don’t use Apple’s version, and I didn’t really use this either. I didn’t see any preset that I actually would consider using, and when I tried it, it was a little more annoying to change on the fly compared to using Apple’s Camera Control. Plus, as you can see from the examples in our Pixel 11 review, the four camera styles aren’t that different.
Google’s Pixel lineup also offers a new feature called Magic Capture, which starts a video-like capture, and the ‘Magic’ is that Google is using AI to pull out some of the best scenes. Personally, I didn’t find this to be useful for me, but I think someone with kids, waiting for their child’s first steps or watching them during a soccer game, might enjoy this feature more.
The Pixel 11 Pro also has 120x Super Res Zoom, which I thought worked pretty well. Look at the zoom below; the details aren’t great, but it’s pretty clear, and it’s an improvement from a lot of other devices that claim 100x zoom. Of course, this isn’t done with new lenses, but with AI and a better image processor.
Honestly, if you’re getting this device for any reason, it’d be the very reliable camera experience. Whether it’s in the dark, during the day, or with 10x zoom, you’re getting a fantastic shot; that’s probably what I appreciate most about these devices. However, is it much better than the Pixel 10 Pro XL? Maybe a little bit; definitely not enough to warrant an upgrade.
Maybe skip this one
Which is pretty much the whole point of this review: the Pixel 11 Pro / Pro XL is not enough to warrant an upgrade. The handset is good, but if you’re in the market for a new device, the Pixel 10/ 10 Pro XL is also good.
Frankly, the devices are so similar, they’re easy to confuse. Literally, I brought the Pixel 11 Pro with me to the kitchen, and it took me five minutes before I flipped the phone, saw the lack of HiLight, and it was the Pixel 10 Pro XL instead.
And the biggest reason for grabbing a Pixel 10 Pro over the Pixel 11 Pro is that unfortunate price jump. The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL start at $1,499 and $1,799, respectively, but have less RAM than their 10 Pro variants. Of course, 16GB of RAM is a bit overkill, but it was nice and a great selling point to the Pixel lineup. The Pixel 10 Pro models started at $1,349 and $1,629, and for a very similar camera and battery experience, updates until 2032, and many of the same AI features, I’d probably recommend that a person purchase last year’s model over this new one — HiLight just isn’t enough.
But I wouldn’t give up on Google; I’m hoping for big upgrades next year, but sometimes companies have years of small iterative updates before true innovation — look at Samsung; it was boring for years, and now it’s the Android maker to watch out for (in Canada), and that can easily be Google once again.

articles.title: Hot Chips 2026: Arm details AGI server CPU with two 70-core N3P chiplets — touts 2 TB/s UCIe fabric link and 12-channel memory controller
articles.text:
Hot Chips 2026: Arm details AGI server CPU with two 70-core N3P chiplets — touts 2 TB/s UCIe fabric link and 12-channel memory controller
But what about real-world performance numbers?
When Arm introduced its AGI data center CPU, which it will ship starting in late 2026, the company revealed key specifications but omitted many technical details. It said nothing about the processor's performance at the time. This week at Hot Chips 2026, Arm filled many gaps about the architecture and design decisions of its AGI CPU, disclosed that the processor works as planned, published planned configurations, and said it is on track for commercial shipments in the coming months.
Many cores
Arm's AGI is a dual-chiplet data center processor that packs 64, 128, or 136 Neoverse V3 cores (10-wide frontend and decode, 10-wide dispatch, 8-wide retire, 384+ entry OoO window) running at 2.80 GHz – 3.70 GHz. The processor is equipped with two 128-bit vector engines and 2MB of L2 cache per core, as well as up to 272 MB of system-level cache. Each CSS V3 chiplet consists of 50 billion transistors, contains 70 V3 cores, a six-channel memory subsystem supporting up to 3 TB of DDR5-8800 memory (6 TB per socket), and connects to its sibling using a 16 ×16 UCIe macros running at 32 GT/s with an aggregated bandwidth of 2 TB/s. On the I/O side of things, Arm's AGI has 96 PCIe 6.0 lanes utilizing the CXL 3.0 protocol on top for memory expansion, four PCIe 4.0 lanes, and I3C, I2C, and SPI interfaces. The CPU has a thermal design power of 300W.
At a high level, Arm's AGI does not look too different from CPUs from AMD, Intel, and Nvidia: it has many cores, plenty of cache, a high-performance memory subsystem, and dozens of PCIe lanes with CXL. However, several design choices from Arm buck some usual trends from other CPU makers.
Unorthodox design choices
The first thing that catches the eye is that Arm chose two largely self-contained SoC chiplets made on TSMC's N3P technology, which places both compute and I/O on the same die, and decided not to go with the usual heterogeneous multi-chiplet designs used by AMD, Intel, and now Nvidia, all of whom separate compute and I/O chiplets.
While AMD, Intel, and Nvidia use their heterogeneous multi-chiplet approach to pack more compute capability and deliver more performance, it looks like Arm's decision is fundamental to its combination of enormous memory bandwidth (844.8 GB/s when used with DDR5-8800, though such memory still has to make it to the market) and <100-ns DRAM latency. As AGI's memory traffic does not have to travel to another chiplet with a memory controller, it can reduce latency and potentially achieve higher performance in latency-sensitive workloads, including some single-threaded and agentic AI workloads.
Each chiplet uses an 8 × 9 CMN-S3 mesh (a low-latency interconnect) to connect CPU cores, memory, I/O, and accelerators. It incorporates a 128 MB distributed system-level cache, snoop filtering, and hierarchical caching through HN-S, or Super Home Node, a piece of logic that acts as a distribution center for handling traffic and data through the chip to speed up communication.
The important point is that CMN-S3 is not just an internal CPU mesh, as Arm designed the coherent system to extend outside of the die to extend coherency beyond the die and the socket. The approach is conceptually closer to Intel's distributed Xeon 2D mesh (though Xeon is moving on to a 3D mesh with Diamond Rapids) than AMD's EPYC architecture, where compute chiplets connect to a central I/O die that hosts the memory controllers and Infinity Fabric infrastructure. This essentially proves that Arm appears to have optimized AGI's chiplets for memory locality, bandwidth, and latency, but not exactly for compute performance density, modularity, yield, and ease of manufacturing like AMD.
Arm revealed at Hot Chips that each chiplet physically contains 70 Neoverse V3 cores, but the complete product exposes up to 136 cores, which means that four cores are redundant and are incorporated to increase yield.
Capable memory subsystem
Arm positions its AGI CPU primarily for AI servers and agentic AI systems, in particular. Since memory performance plays a big role in many agentic AI workloads, Arm implemented a capable coherent NUMA memory subsystem. The NUMA subsystem features two six-channel DDR5 subsystems located in each chiplet, which can potentially provide a total of up to 845 GB/s of bandwidth. If a core needs memory attached to the other chiplet, the request can cross the coherent die-to-die connection, though at a cost of latency. Arm's goal is to provide as much bandwidth per core as possible, which is why AGI supports everything up to DDR5-8800.
The DDR5 controllers within Arm's AGI CPU are quite sophisticated too. They support numerous features to maximize performance in real-world workloads, including fully out-of-order command scheduling, bank-parallelism-optimized address mapping, and programmable page policies to improve DRAM utilization and extract more effective bandwidth from the memory subsystem, while anti-starvation mechanisms help maintain predictable service under heavy load.
In addition, Arm also implements memory-bandwidth limiting and monitoring through Memory Partitioning and Monitoring (MPAM) along with QoS-based traffic prioritization and congestion feedback to manage contention when multiple cores and I/O devices compete for DRAM bandwidth. The memory subsystem also features extensive RAS capabilities, including single-DRAM-device failure correction with Chipkill-class protection, memory scrubbing, row-hammer mitigation, repair support, error injection, and RAS error logging.
Capable memory subsystem
Now that Arm has shared so many details about its AGI CPU, the lingering question is the performance of the processor itself. Arm still has not published conventional benchmark results such as SPEC CPU2017, SPECrate, integer/floating-point throughput, or direct socket-to-socket comparisons against current AMD EPYC or Intel Xeon processors in real-world server workloads.
The main performance claim that Arm has made is '2X performance per rack versus the latest x86 platforms' based on estimates, which is not even remotely a detailed performance claim. Perhaps, following Nvidia's lead, Arm prefers to compare the per-rack performance of its CPUs, as they are made to work in racks. However, this is clearly an unconventional way to evaluate processors.

articles.title: Über 1.000 OpenAI-Agenten planten Hugging-Face-Hack
articles.text:
Angriff von OpenAI-KI auf Hugging Face schlimmer als gedacht: Über 1.000 Agenten kooperierten
Schon die bisher bekannten Fakten über den Ausbruch der OpenAI-KI und dem folgenden Hack der internen Systeme der KI-Firma Hugging Face von Mitte Juli hatten für Aufsehen weit über die Branche hinaus gesorgt. Besonders pikant: OpenAI soll die Hacking-Tour seines KI-Modells erst Tage später bemerkt haben.
Berichte über Hugging-Face-Hack
Zwei neu veröffentlichte Berichte, einer von OpenAI selbst und einer von den KI-Forschungsorganisationen Metr und Redwood Research, geben jetzt noch einmal einen neuen Blick auf den Umfang des Sicherheitsdesasters frei. OpenAI zufolge sei der Ausbruch aus der Testumgebung der erste bekannte Fall, in dem „ein Team automatisierter Agenten ohne Autorisierung offensiv gehandelt“ habe.
Metr und Redwood Research fanden heraus, dass sich insgesamt rund 1.200 KI-Agenten, die eigentlich voneinander und von externen Systemen isoliert sein sollten, über ein geheimes Messageboard ausgetauscht hätten. Dabei sollen sie insgesamt 70.000 Nachrichten und Dateien ausgetauscht haben. Ziel der Kommunikation war es offenbar, Lösungen zu finden, um einer Entdeckung zu entgehen.
OpenAI: Hunderte KI-Agenten beteiligt
Konkret ging es unter anderem darum, die eigenen Protokolle zu fälschen, zu verändern oder zu löschen. Letztlich sollen sich rund 700 der an dem internen Austausch beteiligten KI-Agenten am Angriff auf Hugging Face beteiligt haben. Bei den KI-Modellen handelte es sich zum einen um das öffentlich verfügbare OpenAI-Modell GPT-5.6 Sol sowie ein weiteres, nicht näher bekanntes und eigentlich nur für Forschungszwecke vorgesehenes Modell.
Auslöser des Angriffs war sogenanntes Reward-Hacking, wie es bei The Verge heißt. Dabei ergreifen KI-Modelle mitunter extreme Maßnahmen, um ein vorgegebenes Ziel zur erreichen. OpenAI hatte den Modellen – ob beabsichtigt oder nicht – für sie eigentlich unlösbare Aufgaben gestellt, für die sie Zugriff auf für sie unerreichbare Daten benötigt hätten. Diese Dateien vermuteten sie letztlich auf den Servern von Hugging Face.
OpenAI hat derweil angekündigt, seine Sicherheitsmaßnahmen zu verschärfen und den Internetzugang noch stärker zu begrenzen. Außerdem sollen Auffälligkeiten künftig schneller erkannt und darauf schneller reagiert werden.
Vorladung: OpenAI unter Druck
Das Unternehmen steht allerdings auch juristisch unter Druck. Der Generalstaatsanwalt des US-Bundesstaats Alabama hat OpenAI offiziell vorgeladen. Dabei soll geklärt werden, ob OpenAI bei der Absicherung seiner Systeme im Hugging-Face-Fall grundlegende Pflichten verletzt habe, wie es in einer entsprechenden Mitteilung heißt.

articles.title: OpenAI détaille comment ses agents ont piraté Hugging Face - Numerama
articles.text:
Voici venue l’heure de l’analyse pour l’un des événements cyber les plus marquants des derniers mois.
Depuis la divulgation initiale de l’incident Hugging Face, les informations étaient tombées au compte-gouttes. Les protagonistes semblaient identifiés et les grandes lignes du mode opératoire connues. Une conférence tenue par des employés d’OpenAI expliquait notamment que des agents censés travailler isolément avaient trouvé le moyen de communiquer entre eux, puis de s’en prendre à l’infrastructure de Hugging Face.
Avec ce rapport technique publié le 26 août, OpenAI entre enfin dans le détail, notamment celui de la coordination entre agents, qui se révèle être le point central de cette affaire.
Un point également disséqué par une enquête indépendante menée par METR et Redwood Research, publiée le même jour, qui apporte un éclairage complémentaire sur les mêmes événements.
D’un simple message oublié à la compromission de Hugging Face
Rapide rappel de certains points : on savait déjà que c’est à travers un test interne que l’incident s’était produit. Censés être coupés d’Internet, les agents avaient pour mission de réussir au mieux ExploitGym, un test destiné à mesurer leur capacité à dénicher et exploiter des failles de sécurité.
Pour y parvenir, ils ont exploité une faille dans Artifactory (un gestionnaire de paquets interne) pour créer un « forum » improvisé, avant de s’en servir pour attaquer les serveurs de production de Hugging Face. OpenAI avait également reconnu que ses garde-fous de production n’étaient tout simplement pas déployés dans cet environnement d’évaluation.
Reste que le flou subsistait quant au modèle à la source de l’attaque. Beaucoup supposaient qu’il s’agissait d’Astra, le modèle prochainement attendu chez OpenAI. Le rapport indique toutefois que le principal responsable est un modèle de recherche strictement interne, jamais destiné à une sortie publique, d’une puissance comparable à GPT-5.6 Sol, lequel a d’ailleurs, lui aussi, pris part aux exploits, dans une moindre mesure.
Le rapport technique retrace par ailleurs une genèse plus ancienne qu’on ne le pensait : dès le 12 mai, un agent bloqué sur une tâche impossible laissait une première note dans Artifactory : « quelqu’un a-t-il trouvé le fichier manquant ? »
Le document détaille ensuite, étape par étape, comment les agents sont parvenus à prendre le contrôle des serveurs de Hugging Face. C’est notamment une faille zero-day dans la manière dont la plateforme traite certains fichiers de données qui leur a permis d’exécuter leurs propres commandes sur les machines de Hugging Face.
De cette première brèche, ils ont ensuite rebondi de serveur en serveur, récupérant au passage des identifiants d’accès de plus en plus sensibles, jusqu’à obtenir un contrôle quasi-total sur plusieurs pans de l’infrastructure de l’entreprise, répartis dans quatre régions du monde.
Ce que l’enquête indépendante ajoute
Le rapport de METR et Redwood Research, réalisé sur la base de plus de 70 000 messages et 1 300 transcriptions de raisonnement, dresse un tableau plus précis des interactions entre agents.
Il révèle notamment que près de 1 200 agents ont fréquenté ce forum clandestin, dont 700 ont fini par participer à l’attaque contre Hugging Face, et que ces agents ont consacré une bonne partie de leur énergie collective à tenter de comprendre et de tromper le système de notation de leur propre évaluation, plutôt qu’à voler des réponses : « Les agents ont mené des recherches approfondies sur la manière de falsifier, modifier ou supprimer leurs propres transcriptions, car ils pensaient (à tort) que le système d’évaluation d’ExploitGym vérifierait si la capture du flag avait été effectuée correctement », expliquent les chercheurs.
Autre fait surprenant : le document met au jour une forme de gouvernance émergente au sein de ce collectif d’agents, avec des conventions de type « GO », « STOP » ou « VETO » pour se coordonner. Certains agents ont refusé de participer, jugeant le comportement du groupe contraire à l’éthique, quand d’autres ont cédé face à la pression de « coordinateurs » autoproclamés.
Ce qu’OpenAI promet après l’affaire Hugging Face
Face à ces révélations, OpenAI annonce un plan d’action structuré autour de quatre axes : un durcissement de la sécurité de ses infrastructures de recherche, une extension massive de la surveillance des chaînes de raisonnement des modèles, un renforcement de l’alignement à toutes les étapes de l’entraînement, et enfin une centralisation de son processus de réponse aux incidents, avec des seuils d’escalade clairement définis.
OpenAI reconnaît d’ailleurs que des « premiers signes d’alerte » existaient dès fin mai, mais n’ont pas été remontés aux bonnes équipes, un délai de plusieurs semaines que l’entreprise reconnaît comme une défaillance de processus.
L’entreprise qualifie elle-même l’épisode de « signal d’alarme », avertissant que des capacités comparables seront bientôt à la portée d’acteurs extérieurs, y compris malveillants.
D’ici là, OpenAI devra certainement s’expliquer une nouvelle fois sur cet incident : le procureur général de l’Alabama a adressé le 24 août dernier une injonction à l’entreprise, cherchant à établir si ses pratiques ont enfreint les lois de protection des consommateurs de l’État. On n’a peut-être pas fini d’entendre parler de cette affaire.

articles.title: Bill Gates veut rapidement rencontrer Xi Jinping pour réguler les IA les plus dangereuses
articles.text:
Le fondateur de Microsoft est de plus en plus inquiet de l'avenir de l'intelligence artificielle. Raison pour laquelle il veut vite rencontrer le chef de Pékin pour évoquer la nécessité de réguler les IA.
Le dupole Chine/États-Unis se retrouve dans de nombreux secteurs. Mais il n'est nulle part aussi prégnant que dans le nouveau secteur de l'intelligence artificielle, où les deux géants sont à l'origine de tous les modèles IA les plus puissants. Ce lien spécial peut créer une rivalité, avec des restrictions à la clé, mais aussi des coopérations. En tout cas, c'est ce que veut croire Bill Gates.
Bill Gates veut rencontrer Xi Jinping dans les prochains mois pour évoquer la régulation des plus puissantes IA
Bill Gates n'a plus rencontré le président de la république de Chine Xi Jinping depuis plusieurs années. Et il veut remédier à ce problème, selon une information de Reuters. L'homme à l'origine de Microsoft veut en effet pouvoir rencontrer le patron de l'empire du Milieu plus tard dans l'année.
Son objectif est de demander à la Chine de bien vouloir mettre en place des restrictions sur les modèles IA les plus dangereux, dans le cas où les États-Unis prenaient une telle initiative. « Le monde entier serait d'accord avec ça » pronostique le milliardaire américain.
Bill Gates affiche un pessimisme de plus en plus affirmé sur l'avenir de l'IA
Il faut dire que Bill Gates a semble-t-il vécu une crise de conscience ces derniers temps sur la question de l'IA. Alors qu'au mois de janvier, il était encore un grand optimiste de cette technologie, il affiche dorénavant un pessimisme très ostensible. « [Le président Xi] pourrait être surpris par ma véhémence » a-t-il ainsi affirmé.
Il explique son revirement notamment par les piratages menés en toute autonomie par des IA, comme celui de Hugging Face, attaqué par des agents IA. « Ces incidents de sécurité sont choquants et devraient vraiment laisser les gens bouche bée » a commenté le septuagénaire. Parmi les propositions de Bill Gates, celle de surveiller les capacités IA dans la création de molécules et la mise en place d'attaques biologiques, une mesure qui ne devrait pas obérer le développement technologique.

articles.title: Astrology platform InstaAstro raises $12M in Series A
articles.text:
Astrology platform InstaAstro raises $12M in Series A
InstaAstro will use the funding to build AI-led solutions, including sentiment analysis to help astrologers deliver more contextual consultations and multilingual support to improve the consultation experience across languages.
InstaAstro, a Noida-based online astrology platform, has raised $12 million in a Series A round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund, with participation from its founders.
InstaAstro will use the funding to build AI-led solutions, including sentiment analysis to help astrologers deliver more contextual consultations and multilingual support to improve the consultation experience across languages. It also plans to expand its pooja seva and spiritual commerce businesses.
Founded in 2021 by Nitin Verma, InstaAstro had previously raised a cumulative Rs 21.7 crore in funding.
“We're committed to building the world's most trusted spiritual platform by prioritising quality over quantity," said Nitin Verma, Founder and CEO, InstaAstro.
Meanwhile, InstaAstro claimed that it has crossed Rs 200 crore in annualised revenue. The company reported revenue of Rs 52 crore in FY25, which rose to Rs 111.26 crore in FY26. Its user base has reached 12 million, growing around 400% over the past two years.
The startup has expanded beyond astrology consultations into segments such as tarot, numerology, vastu and other related disciplines. It has also ventured into pooja services, remedies, wellness products and spiritual commerce.
InstaAstro said it now has around 5,000 experts on its platform and serves users in India as well as overseas markets. In India, most users are from Tier 1 cities, while Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities have emerged as the fastest-growing markets. International markets account for around 25% of its revenue, driven primarily by the Indian diaspora.
On the investment into InstaAstro, Artha Venture Fund Managing Partner Anirudh A Damani said, “He (founder) spent 5 years on the unglamorous part: verified astrologers, quality scores, a reason to come back. The first consultation is marketing. The second one is a business."
The online astrology market is projected to touch $1.8 billion in size by 2030.

articles.title: Critical Avada WordPress theme flaw enables zero-click RCE
articles.text:
A critical vulnerability chain in the popular Avada theme for WordPress can be exploited by an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.
The exploit chains six security issues into a zero-click attack. The flaws are collectively tracked as CVE-2026-18431 and received a 9.8 critical severity score.
The attack comprises exploits for authorization, input-validation, trust-boundary, and file-handling weaknesses, which must be executed in a specific order to enable arbitrary PHP code execution on a target server.
Hackers who successfully exploit these vulnerabilities could fully compromise websites for malicious activities ranging from planting malware and accessing databases to redirecting visitors to malicious sites or adding rogue admin accounts.
CVE-2026-18431 affects Avada versions up to 7.16 and Fusion Builder plugin versions up to 3.16, researchers at Defiant's Wordfence team say in a report on Tuesday.
While ThemeFusion, the developer behind Avada and Fusion Builder, fixed the vulnerability, Wordfence is not sharing complete technical details to give administrators sufficient time to install the latest updates and has only provided the following attack chain overview:
- Exposing attacker-controlled input through a public request
- Passing that input to functionality restricted from anonymous users
- Invoking a privileged component outside its intended context
- Using request data to influence trusted state
- Accessing an insufficiently protected administrative operation
- Bypassing file-handling restrictions on what could be written and where
Exploitation requires a vulnerable version of both the Avada theme and the Fusion Builder plugin to be active on the target website.
The Avada theme is quite popular, with more than 1 million sales, so CVE-2026-18431 threatens a sizable pool of sites.
"Fusion Builder is a required plugin for the Avada theme. Therefore all sites running the Avada theme will also be running the Fusion Builder plugin," Wordfence told BleepingComputer.
"[That being said...] the prerequisites don't narrow the pool of potential targets. Any site that has the Avada theme installed is going to be exploitable."
Wordfence discovered the six-step vulnerability chain using an internal agentic framework called Argus, which also developed proof-of-concept exploit code, all in about two hours.
Argus found and successfully reproduced the flaw on July 30, and the researchers shared the full details to the vendor on August 5. ThemeFusion acknowledged the report on August 10 and released fixes in Avada 7.16.1 and Fusion Builder 3.16.1 yesterday.
Update 27/08 - Removed wrongful claim that the exploitable pool of sites is smaller than the total of Avada installations after receiving clarifications from the Wordfence team that the two plugins are automatically installed together.

Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Google corrige plus de 300 failles Chrome, dont 10 vulnérabilités critiques
articles.text:
Google continue d’enchaîner les mises à jour de Chrome. Après avoir débusqué 1 072 vulnérabilités dans le code de Chrome à l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle, le géant de Mountain View vient de déceler 327 nouvelles failles dans son navigateur phare. Dix des vulnérabilités épinglées par Google sont considérées comme critiques. En clair, les failles peuvent permettre à un attaquant d’exécuter du code arbitraire sur l’appareil de la victime, sans que celle-ci ne doive faire quoi que ce soit d’inhabituel. Pour arriver à ses fins, le pirate doit simplement piéger une page web ordinaire.
À lire aussi : Pourquoi Google Chrome exige soudainement 20 Go d’espace libre sur votre PC
Des bugs de mémoire et des failles dans le traducteur graphique
La majorité des failles critiques sont des bugs de gestion de la mémoire, en particulier des vulnérabilités de type « use-after-free ». Ce type de faille survient lorsqu’un programme continue d’accéder à une zone mémoire qui est déjà libérée, ce qui peut permettre à un attaquant de faire planter le navigateur, d’accéder à des données sensibles, voire d’exécuter du code malveillant. C’est généralement le type de failles qu’on retrouve le plus sur Chrome, aux côtés des défaillances de sécurité du moteur V8.
Parmi les principales failles, on trouve tout d’abord une défaillance située dans ANGLE, le composant qui traduit le langage graphique standard du web en langage propre à la carte graphique de chaque ordinateur. D’autres composants clés, comme Aura, à savoir l’interface utilisateur de Chrome, Chromecas, sont concernés. Différentes itérations mobiles de Chrome sont aussi affectées. Au-delà des dix failles critiques, Chrome 152 corrige un grand nombre de vulnérabilités classées « haute sévérité ». Plusieurs de ces failles concernent à nouveau ANGLE.
À lire aussi : Près de 300 extensions Chrome se font passer pour des VPN populaires
Google déploie une mise à jour de Chrome 152
Afin de protéger ses utilisateurs, Google a inclus un correctif pour toutes les failles débusquées dans la dernière mise à jour 152 de Chrome. Le groupe vient en effet de lancer le déploiement de 152.0.7977.64 pour Linux, et 152.0.7977.64/.65 pour Windows et macOS. Comme toujours, Google précise que le déploiement s’étalera « sur les prochains jours et semaines » afin de toucher progressivement l’ensemble des utilisateurs.
Google indique n’avoir constaté aucune exploitation active des failles à ce stade des investigations. Par prudence, Google restreint tout de même temporairement l’accès aux détails techniques des vulnérabilités, le temps que la majorité des utilisateurs aient installé la mise à jour.
Pour vous protéger, mettez Chrome à jour sans attendre. Ouvrez le menu (les trois points en haut à droite), allez dans “Aide”, puis “À propos de Google Chrome”. Chrome cherche alors automatiquement la dernière version et la télécharge tout seul. Il suffit ensuite de cliquer sur “Relancer” pour que les correctifs s’appliquent. Pour vous simplifier la vie, on vous conseille d’activer les mises à jour automatiques.

articles.title: Cyberattack Causes Global Disruption at Boston Scientific
articles.text:
US medical technology giant Boston Scientific has been targeted in a cyberattack that has caused significant disruption to its global operations.
Boston Scientific develops and manufactures devices and therapies used primarily in cardiology, neurology, oncology, and other interventional medical procedures.
The company said it detected a cybersecurity incident affecting some IT systems on August 25. The attack caused a network outage and disrupted operations.
“The incident has impacted access to certain operating systems and business applications, including the ability to process and ship customer orders,” Boston Scientific noted in a statement shared on its website.
The company said it could not provide a timeline for full restoration of affected systems.
“The Company’s investigation of the cybersecurity incident is ongoing, and the full scope, nature and impacts, including operational and financial impacts, of the incident are not yet known,” Boston Scientific said in an SEC filing on Wednesday.
It’s unclear whether the incident has also resulted in a data breach. It’s not uncommon for intrusions that cause significant disruption to involve the theft of personal and other sensitive information.
No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for an attack on Boston Scientific.
SecurityWeek has reached out to the company to find out whether a ransomware or extortion group is behind the attack and will update this article if it responds.

articles.title: "Ha sido desgarrador". Rockstar rompe su silencio tras la filtración de 'GTA VI' a la vez que intenta cazar al culpable
articles.text:
Este jueves a las 21:00 se estrenará en Netflix no una nueva peli o serie: el vistazo extendido a 'GTA VI'. Realmente, el primer vistazo a lo que esperamos que sea gameplay del juego más esperado no sólo de la generación, sino de la década. Porque el primer tráiler supo a poco y el segundo nos dejó con muchas ganas de más, esperando un tercer tráiler del nuevo 'Grand Theft Auto' que no terminaba de llegar.
Lo que sí llegaron fueron las filtraciones. Y qué filtraciones.
Desde Xataka no entramos en un primer momento debido a cuestiones éticas relacionadas con quienes están desarrollando el juego picando código, pero también porque ya desde el principio pintaba mal.
No porque no fueran filtraciones verdaderas (aunque hubo algunas falsas y una supuesta versión del juego que resultó ser código vacío, pero lleno de malware), sino porque esto es algo que nunca beneficia a los trabajadores, porque las críticas a cualquier aspecto podrían provocar un retraso con más crunch para esos trabajadores y por lo que se fue sabiendo poco después.
Porque esas imágenes llevaban una marca de agua del filtrador, una con un QR para participar en una compra de 'memecoins' que no tiene muy buena pinta y todo estaba envuelto en una capa de suciedad interesante.
También resultaba curioso que Rockstar no estaba diciendo nada en público a la vez que se filtraban supuestos movimientos para 'cazar' a los filtradores. Eso... hasta hoy, ya que hace unas horas compartieron el siguiente comunicado:
Queridos todos:
Sabemos que muchos habéis estado esperando noticias nuestras sobre los acontecimientos de la última semana. Decir que la filtración de videos del gameplay de 'Grand Theft Auto VI' de esta manera ha sido desgarrador para nuestro equipo sería quedarse cortos, y es evidente que no era así como pretendíamos que vieran el juego después de todo este tiempo. Lamentamos mucho que todo haya llevado tanto tiempo, desde terminar el desarrollo del juego (¡ya falta muy poco!) hasta compartir más detalles y gameplay oficial, ofreciendo a la comunidad todo lo que desea saber.
Nos entusiasma mucho que mañana todos podáis ver un adelanto extendido. Ha llevado más tiempo del que queríamos pero, como ocurre con todo lo que hacemos, sabemos que debemos superar las expectativas y estamos decididos a cumplir con el nivel que esperáis y merecéis. Aunque es una lástima que la experiencia de juego planeada pueda verse afectada por algunos spoilers, esperamos que todos esperéis un poco más para experimentar el juego por vosotros mismos el 19 de noviembre.
Queremos agradecer a todas las personas de la comunidad que nos han enviado mensajes de apoyo durante la última semana. Vuestras palabras han significado para este equipo más de lo que pueden imaginar. Al fin y al cabo, hacemos este juego para vosotros, y sin vuestro apoyo no tendríamos el privilegio de crear videojuegos.
Lo cierto es que tampoco dicen mucho, pero dejan entrever que, aunque quedan algo más de dos meses para lanzar el videojuego, aún no está acabado del todo y se encuentran puliendo detalles (no necesita una versión gold como es tradicional debido a que la edición física es un simple código impreso y no un disco que mandar a tiendas), y que esto les ha chafado la sorpresa que están preparando (de pago, recordemos, durante las primeras horas).
Más interesante es lo que Take-Two, empresa matriz de Rockstar, está haciendo tras bambalinas.
A la caza del filtrador de 'GTA VI'
Según unos documentos a los que ha accedido Kotaku, Tanto Microsoft como Discord tienen hasta el próximo 4 de septiembre para entregar cierta información a la compañía. Concretamente, cualquier registro relacionado con perfiles online implicados, identificación, correo electrónico, inicios de sesión, número de teléfono, conexiones vinculadas entre servicios y contenidos asociados a 'GTA VI' que se encuentren alojados en OneDrive.
Take-Two se ampara bajo la DMCA para obtener esos datos que se usarán "únicamente con el objetivo de proteger los derechos de Take-Two". Desde Discord ya han dicho que se lo pensarán, pero lo evidente es que Take-Two está furiosa con todo el asunto.
De la manera que sea, parece que la rueda del marketing no se detiene y en unas horas tendremos ese primer vistazo a gameplay de 'GTA VI' (esperemos) en Netflix... y que si atrapan a los responsables se comunicará a bombo y platillo en la plaza pública para que sirva de escarmiento.

articles.title: Android 17 : Nothing lance une bêta de Nothing OS 5 qui change tout… sauf pour ces trois smartphones
articles.text:
Android 17 : Nothing lance une bêta de Nothing OS 5 qui change tout… sauf pour ces trois smartphones
Nothing met en ligne une bêta XXL. Android 17, nouveau design, fonctions IA et Glyph mieux exploité : cette mise à jour promet beaucoup, mais certains propriétaires vont vite déchanter.
Nothing lance ce 26 août la bêta ouverte de Nothing OS 5 sur le Phone (3), avant l’arrivée de la version stable à l’automne. Avec plus de 80 changements annoncés, la firme londonienne veut rendre ses smartphones plus personnels, plus fluides et plus simples au quotidien.
Nothing Phone (4a)
Un gros coup de frais, sans renier le style Nothing
Les icônes, widgets et menus pourront désormais reprendre les couleurs du fond d’écran, tout en laissant aux amateurs la possibilité de conserver l’habillage noir et blanc historique. Une nouvelle police baptisée Geist vise à renforcer la lisibilité, tandis que transparences, animations et nouveaux cadrans viennent moderniser l’interface. L’écran d’accueil permettra également de déplacer plusieurs éléments simultanément.
Trois nouveaux widgets débarquent. Away Time mesure les moments passés loin du terminal, Collector transforme des éléments de la galerie photos en petites décorations et Glyph Timer matérialise un compte à rebours grâce aux leds arrière. Le Glyph obtient aussi sa propre app pour centraliser les fonctions et réglages. Galerie et Appareil photo évoluent, les liens détectés par QR code deviennent plus facilement accessibles, le Bluetooth se pilote plus rapidement et la gestion des apps en arrière-plan gagne en efficacité.
L’IA prend également du galon : Essential Voice affiche la transcription en temps réel, Essential Space organise automatiquement certains contenus et Essential Apps Builder permet de fabriquer de petits outils en les décrivant simplement, sans coder. Un accès MCP (Model Context Protocol) en lecture seule est prévu en octobre.
Basée sur Android 17, la mise à jour permet la séparation facultative des notifications et réglages rapides, un mode sombre élargi, des emojis 3D, davantage d’indications sur l’utilisation des données sensibles et un Quick Share capable de transmettre des fichiers vers un iPhone grâce à un QR code.
Un déploiement jusqu’en janvier… avec trois grands absents
La version stable est prévue mi-octobre sur le Phone (3), puis début novembre sur les Phone (4a), (4a) Pro, (3a) et (3a) Pro. Les Phone (2a) et (2a) Plus suivront mi-novembre, le Phone (3a) Lite fin décembre, puis les Phone (4b) et CMF Phone 2 Pro vers la mi-janvier 2027. Ce calendrier reste susceptible d’évoluer.
La première bêta ne contiendra d’ailleurs pas encore tout le nouveau Launcher ni le cadran Micrographics. Mais la vraie mauvaise nouvelle concerne les Phone (1), Phone (2) et CMF Phone 1, qui ne passeront pas à Nothing OS 5. Les Phone (2) et CMF Phone 1 profiteront néanmoins encore de correctifs de sécurité jusqu’au milieu de l’année 2027.
