articles.title: SpaceX will build a $100 billion Starbase in Louisiana, a 195-square-mile spaceport designed for thousands of annual launches
articles.text:
What we know so far: SpaceX has announced that it plans to build a new $100 billion spaceport on the Louisiana Gulf Coast, and to say it will be massive is an understatement. The company plans to construct the facility across 125,000 acres, or 195 square miles, in an area known as Pecan Island.
SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell said the facility, aptly named Starbase Louisiana, will be a self-sustaining spaceport with propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle-processing facilities, and even an airport.
The site is expected to house five launch complexes with two pads and a propellant farm apiece. That would make it SpaceX's fourth and largest launch site, with the capacity to support thousands of missions per year. Construction is due to begin in 2027, and the first launch is targeted for 2029, according to Louisiana Economic Development.
SpaceX likely chose the location for several reasons: its vast footprint provides room for expansion, the Gulf offers access to a wide range of launch trajectories, and Louisiana's abundant natural gas can supply both power and the methane used by Starship's Raptor engines. Deep-water access would also allow SpaceX to move the enormous vehicles and other hardware by ship.
 – SpaceX (@SpaceX) August 25, 2026
That ambitious launch rate depends on SpaceX making Starship rapidly and fully reusable. It was recently reported that the redesigned Starship V3 completed its first full test flight, while a 2024 milestone saw the company catch a returning Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's giant mechanical arms.
Starbase Louisiana would help launch Starlink satellites, missions to the Moon and Mars, and SpaceX's proposed orbital data centers – a plan that may involve up to one million satellites.
State officials expect the project to create 3,000 direct jobs over a decade with an average salary of $92,600, plus more than 8,100 indirect positions.
Louisiana has offered tax rebates and recruitment assistance, while SpaceX has agreed to make more than $820 million in local payments over 25 years and donate $25 million to a regional community foundation.
Unsurprisingly, the enormous scale of the development has raised plenty of concerns, especially when it comes to environmental implications.
The site occupies fragile coastal marshland close to protected wildlife areas, and residents and conservation groups fear the noise, light, traffic, and construction could harm fisheries, migratory birds, and wetlands that serve as a natural hurricane buffer. Many locals also say they were kept in the dark while officials negotiated the deal.
SpaceX's history suggests that people's concerns could be warranted. The company underestimated the blast effects of Starship's first integrated launch in Texas, which made a crater and scattered debris across the surrounding area. However, the Louisiana project will still face federal licensing and environmental reviews before rockets can fly.
SpaceX says it will develop only a small part of the property, leave large areas untouched, and work with state agencies to restore eroding marshland. It also plans to hold public town halls in the coming months.

articles.title: Alimentos que no sabías que podías cocinar en una freidora de aire: pochoclo, pasta y postres
articles.text:
Existen dudas frecuentes sobre qué alimentos pueden prepararse en la freidora de aire, así como mitos relacionados con la seguridad y la calidad nutricional de los platos.
Según la Academia Española de Nutrición y Dietética, muchas de estas ideas no corresponden con las posibilidades reales que ofrece esta tecnología. Productos como pochoclo, pasta y postres pueden prepararse si se siguen las pautas adecuadas, sin perder practicidad ni equilibrio nutricional.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es posible preparar pochoclo o palomitas de maíz en una freidora de aire
Un mito muy extendido sostiene que la freidora de aire no permite cocinar palomitas de maíz. Según la Academia Española de Nutrición y Dietética, esto no es cierto.
Las palomitas, conocidas como pochoclo, pueden prepararse fácilmente utilizando una pequeña cantidad de aceite de oliva y poca sal. Así se logra un snack con menor contenido de grasas saturadas y sodio en comparación con las versiones tradicionales hechas con mantequilla.
PUBLICIDAD
El procedimiento sugerido consiste en precalentar la freidora de aire a 180°C durante dos o tres minutos, colocar una fina capa de granos de maíz y cocinar entre ocho y diez minutos.
Es importante evitar las bolsas de palomitas diseñadas para microondas, porque sus componentes no son aptos para este tipo de cocción. De este modo, el resultado es un aperitivo saludable si se controla la cantidad de aceite y sal.
PUBLICIDAD
De qué forma se puede cocer pasta en una freidora de aire
La idea de que la pasta no puede cocinarse en la freidora de aire está muy difundida. Sin embargo, los expertos señalan que sí es posible, siempre que se utilicen los accesorios y procedimientos correctos. Es clave usar un molde apto para freidora de aire, llenarlo de agua, añadir la pasta y una pizca de sal.
Para conseguir una textura al dente, se aconseja cocer a 200°C durante quince minutos. Si se prefiere la pasta más blanda, basta con prolongar la cocción dos o tres minutos más.
PUBLICIDAD
Al finalizar, se pueden agregar salsas o condimentos y dejar en el aparato de tres a cuatro minutos adicionales para integrar los sabores. Este método permite preparar platos rápidos y versátiles, sin renunciar a la textura característica de la pasta tradicional.
Cómo hacer postres en la freidora de aire
La afirmación de que la freidora de aire no es útil para la repostería carece de fundamento. Según la autoridad española, este aparato se ha consolidado como una opción versátil para preparar dulces caseros con menos grasa y en menos tiempo.
PUBLICIDAD
El truco consiste en adaptar las temperaturas y los tiempos del horno, reduciendo entre diez y veinte grados la temperatura y revisando el proceso cada cinco o diez minutos.
Para lograr una textura homogénea y esponjosa en bizcochos y brownies, los expertos sugieren precalentar la freidora de aire y utilizar papel de horno o moldes de silicona compatibles. Esta técnica permite experimentar con recetas clásicas y modificar ingredientes para obtener versiones más saludables, sin perder calidad ni sabor.
PUBLICIDAD
De qué forma se puede gratinar preparaciones en La freidora de aire
Otra de las dudas habituales es si la freidora de aire permite gratinar platos como lasaña, macarrones o casseroles. Sí es posible, siempre que se seleccione la función adecuada y se ajusten los parámetros del aparato. Para gratinar, se debe utilizar una temperatura de entre 200°C y 250°C, adaptando el tiempo a cada preparación.
A diferencia del horno, donde se puede observar el avance del gratinado, en la freidora de aire es necesario abrir el aparato cada cierto tiempo para evitar que el queso se queme. Así se obtiene una capa crocante y dorada, con la ventaja de reducir el tiempo de cocción y el consumo de energía.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué cuidados hay que tener con los alimentos congelados
La posibilidad de cocinar alimentos congelados en la freidora de aire genera dudas sobre la seguridad y el resultado final. No solo es posible descongelar pan con la función específica, sino que se pueden cocinar croquetas, verduras y otros productos congelados sin necesidad de descongelar previamente.
Las pautas principales son no sobrecargar la cesta y ajustar la temperatura según el tipo de alimento. Los productos congelados suelen requerir algunos minutos adicionales de cocción para alcanzar la textura deseada.

articles.title: New Twitter launches, says Musk's X gave up the name
articles.text:
Operation Bluebird, the Virginia-based startup trying to revive the allegedly abandoned “Twitter” name and logo, announced Monday that it has launched its new social media network: Twitter.now.
“We are a small company, we have investors, and we have a product,” Stephen Coates, one of Operation Bluebird’s cofounders, told Ars. “And we have waited months and months to launch, and we are not going to wait anymore.”
As Ars reported in December 2025, Coates and his coterie believe that when Elon Musk bought Twitter in 2022 and quickly changed the company’s name to X, the Twitter identity and intellectual property were abandoned.
Musk’s decision, they claim, created the opening for Operation Bluebird to claim Twitter’s trademarks.
But Musk’s X Corporation quickly sued Operation Bluebird late last year and asked a federal judge in Delaware to issue a preliminary injunction to prevent a new version of Twitter from launching.
However, in an April 2026 hearing, US District Court Judge Colm Connolly gave a tentative ruling from the bench that X seemed to have given up intellectual property claims over the word “tweet” and the Twitter bird logo—and possibly even on the word “Twitter” as well. The judge has yet to issue a written order.
For Coates, who serves as Twitter’s new general counsel and previously worked in the same role during the pre-Musk era, the judge’s words were enough to serve as a green light.
“It’s our opinion that X has abandoned its rights on the Twitter and tweet trademarks,” he said.
Still, the new Twitter takes great pains to put daylight between itself and the previous iteration of Twitter.

articles.title: Eindhoven’s VitalFluid raises €17.2 million to protect crops with its "lightning in a box" technology | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Vitalfluid, an Eindhoven-based startup helping growers to adopt plasma technology as a natural, residue-free alternative to chemical fungicides, has secured €17.2 million to accelerate sustainable crop protection worldwide.
The round was co-led by Invest-NL and Alder Tree Investments, with participation from existing shareholders Horticoop, Brabantse Ontwikkelings Maatschappij (BOM), Future Food Fund, Graduate Ventures, Innovation Industries, VDL Groep and Goeie Grutten Impact Fonds. The round also includes a €2.7 million RVO innovation credit. Invest-NL has invested €4 million in this round.
Erik Hertel, CEO of VitalFluid, explained, “This investment confirms the potential of our technology to make a fundamental contribution to a more sustainable and future-proof food system. It allows us to accelerate our commercial rollout and give more growers access to an effective alternative to chemical crop protection.”
Vitalfluid was founded in 2014 by Paul Leenders and Polo van Ooij and is a spin-out from Eindhoven University of Technology. The company specialises in developing Plasma Activated Water (PAW) applications, which provide a sustainable alternative to chemical pesticides and fertilisers.
According to the company, stricter regulations, growing resistance, and rising concerns over biodiversity, water quality, and food residues are driving demand for sustainable alternatives that are effective, cost-competitive, and easily integrated into existing farming practices.
VitalFluid claims to have developed such an alternative. The company transforms water, air, and electricity into plasma-activated water to boost plant health. In a thunderstorm, lightning causes the natural transformation of water into Plasma Activated Water (PAW). The Dutch startup replicates this natural process to create ‘lightning in a box’.
This on-site PAW production provides a natural and sustainable alternative to the pesticides currently used to enhance plant health. VitalFluid mentions that its PAW has proven to be a safe, effective, and scalable solution for safeguarding vegetable cultivation without adverse effects.
The company notes that its machine can isolate and stabilise the reactive nitrogen and oxygen components in Plasma Activated Water, effectively protecting the plant against fungal diseases, without leaving any harmful residues.
VitalFluid reports that following successful commercial adoption by leading UK growers, including Hall Hunter Partnership, Angus Growers and EC Drummond, VitalFluid has already been deployed on more than 100 hectares of commercial strawberry production. This marks an important step from successful trials to large-scale commercial implementation, as per the startup.
Daan Meijer and Florentine Beelaerts van Blokland, investment team at Invest-NL, said, “With this investment, Invest-NL supports a company that contributes to the structural sustainability of agriculture. In this way, we help create a more future-proof food system.”
The company plans to use this capital to accelerate commercial growth in the UK, support expansion into the US market, and enable further rollout in crops such as strawberries, apples, and grapes.
In April 2024, VitalFluid announced that it had secured €5 million in funding to accelerate its market introduction.

articles.title: LibreOffice 26.8 chega para continuar briga com Office; veja as novidades • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
LibreOffice 26.8 chega para continuar briga com Office; veja as novidades
The Document Foundation lançou LibreOffice 26.8 com novidades em ferramentas como Writer (editor de textos) e Calc (planilhas). Suíte é gratuita e tem código aberto.
A The Document Foundation (TDF) escolheu esta quarta-feira (26/08) para lançar oficialmente o LibreOffice 26.8. A nova versão da suíte de escritório gratuita e de código aberto traz novidades em ferramentas como Writer (editor de textos) e Calc (editor de planilhas), além de um pequeno aprimoramento em um recurso opcional de interface.
Confira os destaques da nova versão do pacote a seguir.
Comecemos pela ferramenta que, provavelmente, é a mais popular do LibreOffice. O Writer agora conta com um algoritmo que é mais eficiente na distribuição de espaço entre palavras de textos justificados, evitando que algumas linhas fiquem muito densas e, outras, mais espaçadas.
Além disso, o editor agora detecta automaticamente a direção do parágrafo de textos abertos ou colados, facilitando o trabalho em idiomas escritos da direita para a esquerda, por exemplo.
Agora também há suporte nativo a fontes OpenType variáveis, que permitem ajustar parâmetros como espessura, largura e estilo dentro de uma fonte específica, sem dependência de arquivos separados para cada variação.
O editor de planilhas Calc ganhou o comando Shuffle, que embaralha de modo totalmente aleatório a ordem das células dentro de um intervalo selecionado.
Agora, a ferramenta também é capaz de adicionar campos calculados às tabelas dinâmicas. Na prática, isso permite ao usuário aplicar cálculos personalizados diretamente à tabela dinâmica usando campos já existentes nela como base.
A nova versão também lida melhor com quebras de linha em células referenciadas de arquivos XLSX (Excel) — a TDF continua engajada em aprimorar a compatibilidade dos arquivos do Microsoft Office com o LibreOffice, tanto quanto possível.
Entre os demais atributos do LibreOffice 26.8 estão:
Também é válido destacar que a TDF criticou o painel Ribbon do rival Office recentemente. Para a organização, a Microsoft erra ao oferecer esse tipo de interface única para todos os perfis de usuários.
Sobre esse aspecto, o LibreOffice oferece há tempos uma interface “Tabbed” (baseada em abas) que lembra a abordagem Ribbon, mas é opcional. No LibreOffice 26.8, ela foi mantida, mas com pequenos refinamentos. Um deles é a aplicação de um fundo com cor clara nesse painel. A cor pode ser ajustada.
Em qualquer ferramenta do LibreOffice, a ativação da interface Tabbed ser feita em Exibir / Interface do usuário / Barra de Ferramentas. Ali, escolha “Em Abas” e defina se a mudança será aplicada somente ao aplicativo aberto ou a todos os apps do pacote.
Sobre o “não recurso”, me refiro a uma característica que a TDF fez questão de deixar claro que o LibreOffice não oferece: um assistente de inteligência artificial.
O LibreOffice 26.8 pode ser baixado a partir do site oficial, com pacotes para Windows, Linux e macOS. Se a nova versão não aparecer para você, aguarde, pois a liberação oficial está prevista para hoje.
Convém relembrar que a suíte é gratuita, tem código-fonte aberto e está disponível em cerca de 120 idiomas, incluindo português do Brasil e de Portugal.

articles.title: El nuevo actor de James Bond, a punto de conocerse: estos son los candidatos finales con un nuevo favorito
articles.text:
Amazon MGM Studios ya se encuentra en las fases finales para fichar al nuevo actor de James Bond. Después del final de la saga de Daniel Craig con No Time to Die, la compañía le compró a Michael G. Wilson y Barbara Broccoli el control creativo de la saga. La intención era reiniciar la franquicia con un nuevo intérprete y nuevas aventuras. De hecho, ya han anunciado a Denis Villeneuve (Dune, Blade Runner 2049) como director de la próxima película.
Sin embargo, el tiempo pasa y el nuevo actor de James Bond aún sigue sin conocerse. Aunque, según las informaciones de Page Six Hollywood, esto está a punto de cambiar. Y es que el estudio ha programado unas audiciones para principios de septiembre y, así, cerrar definitivamente el proceso y elegir al próximo intérprete del agente 007.
De hecho, de acuerdo a la misma fuente, la compañía ya tiene una lista final de candidatos. Entre ellos están Jacob Elordi (Euphoria, Frankenstein), Paul Mescal (Normal People, Gladiator II), Harris Dickinson (Triángulo de la trsiteza, El clan de hierro), Jack Lowden (Dunkerque, Slow Horses) o Callum Turner (One Night Only, Animales Fantásticos). Sin embargo, Amazon MGM Studios tendría un principal favorito.
Al parecer, el actor Jack Barton se ha convertido en el candidato principal para ser el nuevo James Bond. El intérprete británico es conocido por sus papeles en las series Heartstopper y Los hombres del S.A.S., además de la película Pobres criaturas o el videojuego Elden Ring, donde le puso voz a Messmer. Ahora, apunta muy alto para dar un salto en su carrera y pasara a ser el siguiente 007. Eso sí, la fuente matiza que el acuerdo aún no está cerrado y todo podría cambiar en las próximas semanas.
El próximo actor de James Bond, más cerca que nunca
Durante mucho tiempo se ha especulado con qué actor tomará el relevo de Daniel Craig y será el nuevo James Bond. Por los titulares del mundo entero han desfilado varios nombres muy potentes, desde Idris Elba hasta Tom Holland, pasando por Glen Powell. De hecho, hubo un rostro muy repetido a lo largo de diferentes épocas, el de Aaron Taylor-Johnson. Varios incluso dieron por hecho que su fichaje se cerraría tarde o temprano.
Pero con el nuevo rumbo tomado por Amazon y por Denis Villeneuve, todos esos nombres parecen haber quedado atrás. Ahora, la compañía debe decidir de una vez por todas si Jack Barton es el actor que buscan como James Bond o si se decantan por alguno de los otros intérpretes mencionados. Lo cierto es que, sea quien sea, generará debate y mucha expectación.

articles.title: This free Toronto art gallery spotlights some awesome local indie games
articles.text:
One Torontonian has come up with a cool way to shine a light on the city’s talented game development scene.
From illustrator, designer and art director Gavin McCarthy comes Art of the Concept, a free art gallery at George Brown Polytechnic’s North Gallery featuring Toronto indie games that debuted in partnership with this year’s annual Toronto Games Week. McCarthy has since extended the gallery, telling me that it will be there for the rest of August and at least partway into September until whenever the college needs the space once the new school year ramps up.
What an amazing turnout!
Thank you to everyone who came out to yesterday’s reception for Art Of The Concept. It was a wonderful afternoon filled with fantastic conversations about art and video games. A special thanks to the friends, family, volunteers and studios who helped make it happen
#TGW26
— artoftheconcept.bsky.social (@artoftheconcept.bsky.social) June 15, 2026 at 11:50 AM
In the exhibit, you can see key artwork from a bunch of Toronto games with some additional information on each alongside gameplay footage on adjacent TVs. Here are the nine featured games:
- Ambrosia Sky (Soft Rains)
- Astronomics (Numizmatic)
- Below (Capybara Games)
- The Big Con (Mighty Yell)
- Capy Castaway (Kitten Cup)
- Curse of Resthaven (Hilltop Studios)
- DuneCrawl (Alientrap)
- Echo Generation (Cococucumber)
- Neo Harbor Rescue Squad (BancyCo)
I unfortunately missed the gallery in June amid all kinds of other events (including FIFA, Dead by Daylight‘s 10th anniversary event and Game Con Canada), but I finally got to check it out this week and loved what I saw. Having this exhibit at a college that people, especially students, can just pop into at no cost is an excellent way to spotlight local indie games. I’ve long said we need more consumer gaming events in Canada to raise awareness of our world-class gaming industry, and Art of the Concept shows how grassroots efforts can very much help fill these gaps.
Shoutout to McCarthy for organizing this and to all of these talented teams for taking part. Definitely worth checking out if you’re in Toronto!

articles.title: Medical device maker Boston Scientific says a cyberattack is causing a 'global disruption' to its operations | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A cyberattack on U.S. medical device maker Boston Scientific is causing an ongoing “global disruption” to its operations, according to a federal regulatory filing on Wednesday. This is the latest health tech giant to face a cyberattack in recent weeks.
The Massachusetts-based company, which makes medically implanted devices like pacemakers and defibrillators, confirmed in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that on Tuesday it began experiencing “disruptions and limitations of access” to its IT systems and business applications critical for its operations.
Boston Scientific said the cyberattack has affected its ability to ship and process orders, but has not said whether the disruption extends to customers with medical devices and implants.
When asked by TechCrunch, Boston Scientific spokesperson Chanel Hastings shared the company’s public statement but would not comment on whether patients are affected by the cyberattack, say what steps patients should take, or answer questions about the nature of the incident.
Boston Scientific treats around 48 million patients a year, according to its website.
The company’s public statement said that its investigation is ongoing and that a timeline for its restoring its systems is not yet known.
It’s not clear what caused the cyberattack at Boston Scientific. Local media in Ireland reported that thousands of staff across Boston Scientific’s campus in Cork were sent home on Tuesday after network communications were cut across the company.
Boston Scientific is the latest health technology company to have been hacked this year, including medical device makers Abbott Laboratories and Medtronic. Earlier this year, Iranian-backed hackers were blamed for a cyberattack on U.S. medical device maker Stryker, which allowed the hackers to remotely wipe tens of thousands of employee devices across its Windows network by abusing a centralized device management portal provided by Microsoft.
According to public internet records, Boston Scientific relies largely on Microsoft and Amazon Web Services for its corporate infrastructure.

articles.title: Leak enthüllt: So viel verdienen Mitarbeiter bei Microsoft
articles.text:
Geleakte Daten zeigen: So viel verdient man bei Microsoft
Der Kampf der großen Tech-Konzerne um Marktanteile im KI-Zeitalter ist auch ein „War for Talents“, ein Wettstreit um die besten Mitarbeiter:innen. Die Firmen sind bereit, für gute Leute tief in die Tasche zu greifen.
600 Microsoft-Mitarbeiter:innen teilten Gehalt und Boni
Dies zeigt einmal mehr eine geleakte interne Tabelle von Microsoft, die das Wirtschaftsmagazin Business Insider einsehen konnte. Die Datei zeigt nicht nur das jährliche Grundgehalt an, sondern auch Gehaltserhöhungen, Bonuszahlungen und Aktienpakete. Letztere sind in manchen Fällen fast so hoch wie das Gehalt.
Etwa 600 Mitarbeiter:innen sollen freiwillig an der Auflistung teilgenommen haben, um Transparenz bei den Gehältern zu befördern. Bei insgesamt rund 220 Beschäftigten des Tech-Giganten ist dies also nur ein kleiner Querschnitt.
Business Insider weißt darauf hin, dass Angestellte mit hohem Einkommen möglicherweise weniger zu der Tabelle beigetragen haben als die Kolleg:innen auf niedrigeren Gehaltsstufen. So könnte die tatsächliche Vergütung im Durchschnitt höher liegen als hier angegeben. Zudem habe das Magazin Ausreißer nach oben oder unten, die auf Tippfehlern basieren könnten, getilgt.
Bis 135 000 Dollar auf niedrigster Gehaltsstufe in Tabelle
Microsoft teilt die Belegschaft nach Leveln ein. Die niedrigste Stufe, die im Leak auftaucht, ist Level 59. Um welche Jobs es sich dabei handelt, ist aus dem Leak nicht ersichtlich. Laut dem Magazin Futurism, das die Tabelle auswertete, könnte es sich um Software-Ingenieur:innen in Einstiegspositionen handeln. Microsoft zahlt laut Futurism besser als der Durchschnitt auf der Einsteigerstufe für Entwickler:innen, der bei 105 000 Dollar liege.
Das Grundgehalt auf dem niedrigsten Level variiert zwischen 111 000 und 134 000 US-Dollar. In Euro sind das 95 000 bis 114 000. Zum Vergleich: Das durchschnittliche Jahresgehalt in den USA lag 2025 bei 53 000 Dollar. Der Cash-Bonus liegt auf Stufe 59 zwischen 0 und knapp 18 000 Dollar. Aktienpakete bringen 0 bis 10 000 Riesen.
Bis zu 300 000 Dollar in Aktien auf höchster Stufe
Die höchste Stufe, die in der Tabelle abgebildet wird, ist Level 67. Das Grundgehalt rangiert hier zwischen rund 240 000 und 280 000 Dollar. Bonuszahlungen bringen zusätzlich zwischen 45,3 000 bis 110 000 Dollar. Aktienpakete begingen hier bei 140 000 Dollar und enden in der Spitze bei 300 000 Dollar. Sie können also höher sein als das Gehalt.
Höchstes und niedrigstes Gehalt bei Cloud + KI
Business Insider dröselt die Vergütungsdaten außerdem nach Teilbereichen und Organisationen auf, von Azure bis Xbox. Da dort allerdings Mitarbeiter:innen aus verschiedenen Gehaltsstufen zusammengefasst werden, ist diese Auflistung nicht besonders aussagekräftig.
So finden sich im Sektor Cloud + KI mit 111 000 Dollar sowohl das niedrigste, mit 450 000 Dollar aber auch das höchste Grundgehalt der Auflistung. Die Aktienprämien rangieren von bescheidenen 9000 Dollar bis zu schwindelerregenden 1,4 Millionen US-Dollar.

articles.title: Wanted: Token spend control and governance without slowing down agentic AI innovation
articles.text:
Wanted: Token spend control and governance without slowing down agentic AI innovation
AI governance and cost control for agentic AI
Scary AI spend and weak access security controls are the flipside of the sharp rise in agentic AI. The answer lies in the form of a control plane that provides the visibility CIOs need.
The past couple of years have seen enterprises press the fast-forward button on generative AI strategies. e have all seen a remarkable change in deployment patterns from useful chatbots to autonomous agents that engage deeply with core software, data and LLMs, and even create their own offspring agents.
CIOs and others are rightly excited about the capacity of agentic AI to reduce manual processes and accelerate speed to insight and actions.
However, governance and AI token costs are alarming challenges.
SVP EMEA at Nutanix.
What’s needed today then is the power of AI without the major concerns over incurring access control risks relating to ‘Shadow AI’ and agent sprawl, and without the ‘bill shock’ relating to unmanaged token consumption.
Moving fast
The generative AI shift that has occurred so quickly spans the early days of ad hoc AI experimentation via testing and pilots to today’s enterprise-grade business processes. It has also outpaced the progress of the usual governance frameworks and effectively rendered them obsolete.
Experienced CIOs may compare the change to the early days of cloud computing platforms when staff with credit cards expensed the AWS trials they had spun up and quickly ran up staggering bills.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Or they may hark back to the days when sales leaders set up online CRM platforms or other process owners bypassed IT to run their own Sharepoint systems.
Or, to reach for yet another lesson from history, they may compare what is happening with generative AI now with the advent of bring-your-own-device schemes and WiFi.
Remember when the user-led demand to have the shiny new gadget ran a coach and horses through the command-and-control IT regimes of cloned PCs stamped with a single image and CIOs no longer managed everything that touched their systems?
The problem is here. Deal with it
However we make the comparison, it’s clear that today there are very real risks relating to data leakage, compliance standards and IT costs because of the speed with which AI has advanced. Nobody wants to lose a chance to gain a competitive advantage and even to fundamentally re-engineer and automate expensive, error-strewn manual processes. So CIOs are once again being asked to square a circle.
As IDC has said: “There is a well-established playbook for calculating the return on an IT investment. Define a baseline, model the efficiency gains, project the cost savings, and present a number to the CFO. For most technology investments, that approach works. Agentic AI breaks it.”
Agentic AI is not fixed and predictable so it’s tough to manage and calculate return on investment, but we know it can take out swathes of cost, so we have to use it and we have to manage costs as best we can.
Gartner has already suggested that by 2027, more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled due to factors such as cost overrun fears or inadequate risk management. That’s not good enough. Corporate IT must step up and deliver the value the business needs, just without the attendant risks and costs.
The solution here is to head off undesirable outcomes at the pass by providing a check, a little like an airport security system that identifies passengers and scans for any potentially unsafe activity or nearby environmental factors such as possession of sharp objects.
You will see this happen in IT very quickly now, such are the risks and speed of what is happening. If 2026 is the year of agentic AI, then it also has to be the year of secure agentic AI.
Enter the AI gateway
One way to address the challenges outlined above is to create a gateway or filter. This approach offers a single control layer regardless of whether the AI model is hosted in public or deployed as a private, self-hosted entity. It effectively secures traffic from agents to LLMs and from MCP servers. This in turn enables organizations to have centralized policies and a clear view of token accounting.
It even has the visibility impact of informing decisions of non-techies who know little about AI operations. So, for example, a CIO working in tandem with a CFO perhaps may identify a better cost efficiency (for example, switching from a hosted model to a private model) and act accordingly.
That’s great news for CIOs who want to maintain a reputation for IT being agents of change but not its less desirable reputation for being risky and pricey.

articles.title: Why Automation Is Essential to Achieve EU CRA Compliance - EE Times
articles.text:
Many companies are still unfamiliar with the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), and even among those that are aware of it, there are significant misconceptions about both its scope and the amount of work required to achieve conformity. Some still view the CRA as a future-focused regulation that primarily affects new products developed after its obligations apply in December 2027. That is a dangerous misunderstanding. The practical question is not whether a product was originally designed in 2027, 2020, or 2012, but whether a product with digital elements will continue to be placed on the EU market after the CRA goes into effect. For large manufacturers, this can bring thousands of existing and legacy products into scope, including products designed long before cybersecurity was treated as a formal requirement. Conforming those products is also far more than a documentation exercise: each connected product requires a cybersecurity risk assessment, implementation of security features based on that assessment, technical-conformity documentation, vulnerability-handling processes, and a support-period strategy. For companies with large product portfolios, understanding the true scale of this effort is one of the first and most important steps toward CRA readiness.
The Scope of the CRA
The European Commission describes the CRA as applying to hardware and software products with digital elements made available on the EU market.
So, are your products in scope? A simple starting point is this: if the product is software or hardware and it has a data connection, it will be in scope. That connection can be direct or indirect. It can be logical or physical. It does not have to look like a classic internet-connected IoT device. That means the CRA applies to software products, embedded systems, industrial devices, consumer devices, networking products, hardware components, and semiconductors when they meet the connectivity test. In other words, the CRA is not just an IoT regulation. It is a broad product cybersecurity regulation applicable to any connected software and hardware that is not already covered under existing regulations such as UNECE’s R.155 cybersecurity for vehicles and the EU’s Medical Device Regulation (MDR).
Once a product is in scope, the manufacturer must do much more than run a scanner or create an SBOM. The CRA requires a product-level conformity workflow. For each product, the manufacturer needs to:
- determine whether the product is in scope
- determine whether it falls into the default, important, or critical categories
- perform a cybersecurity risk assessment
- determine which cybersecurity requirements apply and how they are or will be implemented
- generate a SBOM and disposition any vulnerabilities found
- generate and maintain technical documentation, and
- complete the appropriate conformity assessment process before placing the product on the EU market.
Two Annexes That Define the CRA Workload
Two CRA annexes are especially important for understanding why achieving product-level conformity becomes such a large workload.
Annex I contains the essential cybersecurity requirements:
- Part I addresses product cybersecurity features that are required, such as protection against unauthorized access, confidentiality, integrity, availability, and secure update capabilities.
- Part II addresses vulnerability handling during the support period and relates to both processes within a company as well as the features in the device or software.
The Commission summarizes Annex I as the list of essential cybersecurity requirements that manufacturers must satisfy when designing, developing, producing, and supporting products with digital elements.
Annex VII defines the technical documentation that must be created and kept available for market surveillance authorities. This documentation is the evidence package that shows what the product is, how it was assessed, what requirements apply, and how the manufacturer demonstrates conformity. The CRA states that manufacturers must draw up technical documentation before placing a product with digital elements on the market and then keep that documentation available to authorities for 10 years after the product is placed on the market.
This Is Where the Portfolio Problem Begins
For a company with a small number of products, manual CRA readiness is possible.
But for a company with hundreds or even thousands of products, the number of products multiplied by the number of required tasks creates a workload that results in many person-years of work. Each product requires a category determination, threat and risk assessment, Annex I requirement mapping, internal review, and evidence management, as shown in Figure 2. Some artifacts can be reused across product families, but every product still needs a defensible product-specific record. Even a modest amount of effort becomes enormous at portfolio scale. If the portfolio is complex, poorly documented, or full of legacy products that have limited cybersecurity, that hourly total can rise astronomically.
The exact effort depends heavily on the makeup of a company’s product portfolio. A company with many unique architectures will require more time. A company with strong product-family reuse will require less time. For a portfolio where roughly 10% to 15% of the products are core products and the rest are derivatives where CRA artifacts can be reused, a reasonable planning estimate is still about 30 to 50 hours of work per product on average for execution of the CRA workflow. For 1,000 products, that means 30,000 to 50,000 hours. At roughly 1,700 actual working hours per person-year, that equates to about 18 to 30 person-years of work. For larger portfolios, the problem is multiplied.
These estimates also assume the organization already understands the EU CRA, cybersecurity engineering & methodologies, and how to generate technical security controls. They do not include the time required for personnel to learn the regulation, interpret evolving guidance, train product teams, or become proficient in cybersecurity risk methods. They also do not include product redesign if the risk assessment reveals cybersecurity feature gaps.
So, can your organization find people who understand the regulation and product cybersecurity and staff the task, meeting the mandated deadline of December 11, 2027? Probably not. Finding folks who understand product cybersecurity is challenging as it is very different from enterprise cybersecurity. Here’s where AI and automation step in.
AI and Automation Make the Task Feasible
AI-driven automation significantly changes the scope of the task by reducing the time needed to complete the CRA workflows. Instead of asking engineers or compliance teams to start every product from scratch, an automation platform can process product documentation, such as a data sheet or user manual, and quickly generate a view of whether the product is in-scope or out-of-scope. It considers the intent of the product, interfaces, connectivity, software or hardware characteristics, and other facts needed for the first stage of CRA analysis. It subsequently generates the required threat and risk assessment, maps relevant cybersecurity requirements to reduce risk, and creates documentation.
The most important time savings come from eliminating repetitive manual work. A human expert should not need to follow the same threat-model and risk assessment process hundreds of times. A product-security lead should not need to manually reconstruct similar Annex I mappings for every product variant. A compliance team should not need to build technical documentation packages from scratch every time a product family has a derivative.
Automation allows the organization to create structured product records, reusable analysis patterns, consistent ratings of risk, and documentation outputs. The humans still make the important decisions. They review the generated analysis, correct assumptions, confirm technical facts, approve risk conclusions, and decide what product gaps need remediation. Automation does not remove cybersecurity expertise from the process. It makes that expertise go much further.
Bridging the Expertise Gap with a Boost from Automation
Automation is especially important because most large companies operate with an organizational structure that has a single central cybersecurity team and many product development teams. The central security or compliance team usually understands the regulation best, but they are bandwidth limited. The distributed development and business teams understand the products best and need to make the tradeoffs if investments are needed to reach conformity. A manual approach puts both groups in a tenuous position. The central team cannot manually produce and normalize every risk assessment and technical file across the entire portfolio. The distributed teams do not have the time or bandwidth to become experts in the complex CRA regulation and assessing conformity.
A better operating model is for the central team to use automation to generate all needed CRA information at scale. The distributed product/business teams then review the generated output. They correct product-specific assumptions, clarify the intent of the device, and make product-related gap and remediation decisions. This model leverages centralized CRA expertise while still relying on the products/business teams to make decisions that impact products. It also gives the organization a consistent workflow instead of asking each business unit to invent its own spreadsheet-based process.
Preparing to Leverage Automation
Companies that want to move quickly should not begin by trying to manually write technical files for every product. The better first step is to prepare the portfolio for automated analysis. Step one is simple: gather available documentation for all products including those that may be in scope and products that may be out of scope. Step two is to use automation to process those documents and identify which products are actually in scope for the CRA. That gives the organization a practical starting point instead of forcing teams to inspect every product manually. Step three is to run a pilot for a small number of representative products. The goal of the pilot is to generate threat and risk assessments, understand what security information the CRA requires, identify common documentation gaps, and learn how the review process should work.
This does not need to be a year-long readiness exercise. A company can gather basic product documents, process a representative set of products, and begin understanding its CRA exposure in a matter of weeks. That early work gives leadership a much clearer view of the portfolio: which products are impacted and how much work will it take to bring the portfolio into conformity. It also helps the central product-security and compliance teams build a repeatable operating model before the full portfolio workload arrives.
The EU CRA’s impact comes from the combination of broad scope and product-by-product conformity work. Software, hardware, connected systems, embedded devices, semiconductors, industrial products, consumer devices, and networking equipment can all be pulled into the CRA’s large net when they have digital elements and data connections. For companies with large portfolios, the problem is not simply understanding the regulation. The problem is applying it across thousands of products, many of which were designed before cybersecurity was treated as a core product requirement. Manual work may help companies begin, but it cannot scale the hours, consistency, and documentation required for portfolio-wide conformity. The number of hours required for a large portfolio can reach above 30 person years; this is not only schedule prohibitive given the EU CRA deadline, it also has a huge financial impact, with costs potentially reaching in the multi-millions of dollars range. Automation is the practical path to determining impact, generating risk assessments, identifying required security controls, and moving large portfolios toward EU CRA readiness.

BG Networks can help you accelerate the path to EU CRA compliance with their cybersecurity automation platform, AITHRA.

articles.title: Meta agrees to $18 billion settlement over teen social media harms
articles.text:
Meta has reached a proposed settlement worth up to approximately $18 billion with a bipartisan coalition of 52 attorneys generals over allegations that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to encourage compulsive use by children and teenagers.
The settlement, which is awaiting court approval, resolves a lawsuit filed in 2023 by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general.
The lawsuit accused Meta of designing features that drove compulsive use among young users while misleading users, families, and the public about the risks of its platforms.
The attorneys general also alleged that Meta illegally collected and used data belonging to children under 13, violating federal and state laws, including the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), California's False Advertising Law, and California's Unfair Competition Law.
Under the agreement, Meta will introduce new restrictions for users under 18 on Facebook and Instagram, including a default two-hour daily usage limit that can only be turned off with parental permission. If YouTube and TikTok agree to similar terms, that limit would be reduced to one hour.
Meta will also block teens from using its apps between midnight and 6 a.m. by default and mute most notifications between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. and during school hours, which a parent can modify. Direct messages and some account security or safety alerts are excluded from some of these restrictions.
Other requirements include hiding like and reaction counts from teenagers, blocking cosmetic surgery filters, providing an option for a non-personalized feed, strengthening parental supervision tools, and deploying additional age-verification technology to identify users under 18 and remove children under 13.
An independent auditor will also oversee Meta's compliance with the agreement, while the company will be prohibited from making false or misleading claims about its safety features.
Meta says the agreement includes approximately $18 billion in payments over ten years. Participating states are set to receive roughly $12.7 billion.
Another $5.3 billion will only be released if YouTube and TikTok adopt similar changes, including one-hour daily limits, nighttime restrictions, and age-assurance measures, and each makes a matching payment.
"The agreement is designed to drive industry-wide adoption, ensuring teens receive consistent protections across the apps they use most, like YouTube and TikTok. If industry peers adopt this new standard, certain provisions will be strengthened," announced Meta.
Of this money, California expected to receive between $1.5 billion and $2.1 billion.
"How a significant portion of the payment received by California will be spent will ultimately be decided by the Legislature and Governor, but in the proposed settlement it is earmarked for purposes related to the prevention or remediation of mental health or other harms to young Californians associated with social media use," explains the press release by Attorney General Bonta.
Meta said it expects to incur approximately $10 billion in legal expenses related to the agreement in the third quarter of 2026
Most of the new protections must remain in place for ten years, and the agreement also establishes an independent research foundation focused on teen well-being and social media use.

articles.title: SugarStrings.ai uses simple cheek swabs to identify thousands of genetic disorders
articles.text:
SugarStrings.ai uses simple cheek swabs to identify thousands of genetic disorders
Bengaluru-based healthtech startup SugarStrings.ai has developed a non-invasive DNA test that screens users for more than 7,442 genetic disorders, and aims to make genetic testing more accessible and privacy-focused.
For years, Tony Jose worked in genomics research and diagnostics, studying how genetic conditions shape human health. During his time as CEO of Clevergene Biocorp, one observation kept returning. Many genetic disorders may be classified as rare, but together they affect far more people than most people realise.
“Genetic disorders are essentially rare diseases. But while they are individually rare, as a group it becomes a burden on the population. For instance, hypertension is considered a lifestyle disease now but there are cases of genetic conditions that can lead to its onset,” Jose tells YourStory.
That insight led Jose and Rajasekhara Reddy Ravuri, then Chief Scientific Officer at Clevergene Biocorp, to launch Bengaluru-based SugarStrings in 2023. The startup takes its name from DNA’s sugar backbone (deoxyribose), and aims to help people better understand their genetic predisposition to disease through a single DNA test.
“We realised SugarStrings would be the best way to actualise our idea for the mainstream, enabling people to screen themselves, understand their genetic predispositions, and work on preventing or managing them,” says Jose, now CEO of SugarStrings.
Apart from Jose and Ravuri, the six-member founding team includes co-founder Dhaneesh Jameson. While Jose and Ravuri have stepped away from executive roles at Clevergene Biocorp, Jose continues to serve as its director.
A single test for thousands of disorders
SugarStrings’ flagship product, Healthstring, is a DNA sequencing test that analyses a cheek swab sample to screen for more than 7,442 genetic disorders in a single test.
Unlike blood-based tests, the company uses cheek swabs for sample collection.
"The non-invasive approach is easier for sample collection, bypasses challenges like cold chains, and has a psychological advantage—people are more proactive about their health when they can self-collect samples," Jose says.
In the last five years, the cost of DNA sequencing has become roughly one-third of what it used to be. The test now costs Rs 58,000, with reports delivered between five days and one month.
According to Jose, the company goes beyond identifying an individual's likelihood of developing a condition.
“We don’t just provide the likelihood of developing a disease. We go through the DNA sequencing, find the exact mutation, and create a detailed report on all the possible diseases that can come from that mutation. The report is such that clinical action can be taken referring to it,” he says.
HealthString screens for 7,442 disorders, including 188 hereditary cancers and 302 cardiovascular diseases. By comparison, Jose says New York-based Nucleus Genomics screens for around 2,100 disorders, while Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences screens for about 250.
The company has deliberately chosen to offer a comprehensive test rather than condition-specific screening.
“The key reason we are sticking with a comprehensive test is because the human body is a connected system where diseases affecting a primary organ can have effects on overall function of the body,” Jose says.
He adds that the test can become more affordable as DNA sequencing becomes cheaper and larger volumes and technology implementations come into play.
Another area the startup is focusing on is improving genetic analysis across diverse populations. Many global genetic databases are built largely on data from people of European ancestry, which can make it harder to identify disease-causing mutations in other populations.
SugarStrings says its proprietary machine learning-based crawler identifies novel mutations with 94.89% accuracy, allowing it to analyse genetic data across more diverse populations.
Scaling and future plans
SugarStrings began operations in the last financial year, and has served around 100 clients while validating its technology with more than 1,800 patients.
“This year, we aim to scale to 1,000 customers,” Jose says.
To support that growth, the startup has partnered with hospitals, including Narayana Health and Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru, as well as Aster Medcity in Kochi.
Dr Nalanda Jayadev, Regional CEO, Central Kerala & Aster Medcity, believes genetic screening could change the way healthcare is delivered, by shifting focus from treatment to prevention.
“Instead of waiting for disease to manifest, we can identify individual risks early, intervene proactively, and tailor prevention and treatment to each person’s unique genetic profile,” he says. “This transformation will make healthcare more predictive, precise, and patient-centric, improving outcomes while using resources more wisely.”
“In many ways, genomics and precision care will do for 21st-century medicine what imaging did for the 20th century; it will fundamentally change how we understand, prevent, and treat disease,” he adds.
Jose says SugarStrings is seeing traction from doctors on preventive DNA screening. “At this stage, we have 80% of our consumers coming directly. This will slightly change as we go forward with collaborations with five more hospitals.”
Protecting genetic data
As genetic testing becomes more widely adopted, concerns around data privacy have also grown, particularly after the breach at genetic testing company 23andMe that affected 6.9 million users.
Jose says protecting sensitive genetic information has been a priority from the outset.
“We decentralise data to minimise hacking risks and comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines. We are compliant to local certifications as well such as those under Karnataka Private Medical Establishment Act for offering diagnostic solutions,” he says.
What’s next?
Bootstrapped with an investment of Rs 3 crore, SugarStrings generated Rs 20 lakh in revenue during its first year of operations. The startup is targeting annual revenue of Rs 4.5 crores this year.
It plans to raise $1 million to invest in R&D, improve its platform for doctors and patients, and expand into the UAE, South Africa, Australia, and Canada.
Grandview says the market for genomics companies in India is currently valued at $482 million and projected to reach $1.8 billion by 2033. This implies that the scope for revenue is progressively favourable for companies like SugarStrings if they scale properly.
The founder believes advances in genomics and artificial intelligence will continue to reshape healthcare.
“Hospitals and doctors are increasingly adopting advanced diagnostics techniques and AI-driven tools. We’re seeing rising interest in technology for better patient outcomes,” Jose says.

articles.text:
Intersport est une vraie référence en matière de vélos électriques avec sa marque Nakamura, tout comme Decathlon avec ses Rockrider. Si vous aimez une bonne sortie à vélo mais n’avez pas forcément envie de fournir un effort démesuré, c’est un bon compromis. Le Nakamura Crossover S est une bonne porte d’entrée en la matière, c’est un VTC électrique simple, disponible en trois tailles mais un seul prix : moins de 800 euros avec cette promo.
Les atouts du Nakamura Crossover S
- Les freins à disque hydrauliques à l’avant et à l’arrière
- La batterie de 375 Wh est amovible, pour faciliter la charge
- La fourche suspendue améliore le confort sur les pavés et petits chemins
Le Nakamura Crossover S passe de 1 199,99 euros à 799,99 euros sur le site d’Intersport. Vous pouvez ensuite vous renseigner auprès de votre région pour demander une aide et ainsi alléger la facture encore plus.
Jusqu’au 31 Août, le LUBA 3 AWD 3000 perd 200 € ! Technologie de navigation Tri-Fusion, LiDAR 360°, performances tout-terrain, il planifie ses itinéraires de manière intelligente, propose une tonte puissante et évite plus de 300 obstacles. Bref, ne tondez plus en 2026 !
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Nakamura Crossover S. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un bon premier vélo électrique pour débuter
Avec le Nakamura Crossover S, Intersport se positionne sur le segment des premiers prix, ce qui est idéal pour débuter. C’est un modèle adapté pour tout le monde, avec ses trois tailles, et son cadre bas est particulièrement appréciable puisqu’il est facile à enjamber pour monter dessus. Son look est sobre, avec des lignes simples, ce qui explique aussi son prix de départ raisonnable. La batterie est à moitié intégrée dans le tube diagonal et on peut la retirer pour la charger, ce qui est plus pratique que d’avoir à brancher le vélo tout entier.
Son équipement est complet, avec des garde-boues de série. Mais il n’y a pas de porte-bagages d’origine, ce qui peut éventuellement vous freiner si vous cherchez un vélo pour aller au travail, par exemple. Néanmoins, rien ne vous empêche d’en installer un après l’achat, même si ça implique de devoir repasser à la caisse. Mais il y a des œillets dédiés sur le cadre arrière, donc c’est tout à fait possible.
Une fiche technique correcte pour une entrée de gamme
Le Nakamura Crossover S embarque un moteur de 250 W situé dans le moyeu arrière, avec un couple maximal de 45 Nm, ce qui est, il faut le dire, dans la moyenne basse des VAE actuels, mais suffisant pour la ville et les petites côtes. L’assistance est gérée par un capteur de rotation (aussi appelé capteur de pédalage), et non par un capteur de couple. Donc le moteur se déclenche quand les pédales tournent, avec une sensation d’assistance moins fine et réactive que sur les modèles avec capteur de couple.
Le vélo propose cinq niveaux d’assistance, avec une vitesse maximale légale de 25 km/h. La promesse est de 60 km d’autonomie en mode Eco, mais comme toujours, ce chiffre est lié à d’autres facteurs comme la météo, la route ou le conducteur. Il vaut mieux compter sur lui pendant 40 à 50 km pour être plus réaliste. Il y a 7 vitesses, un petit écran LCD sur le guidon et des pneus de 28 pouces renforcés pour assurer le confort. Vous l’aurez compris, tout est dans la moyenne basse, ce qui explique son prix et le fait qu’il soit recommandé pour débuter et découvrir la discipline.

articles.title: Alfonso Muñoz, experto en jubilación: "Compensa no solicitar la jubilación anticipada si cobras el subsidio para mayores de 52"
articles.text:
Un estudio de la Fundación BBVA e IVIE revela unos datos demoledores sobre la realidad de la masa laboral de España en 2026: ya hay mayor proporción de desempleados con más de 55 años (9,8%), que entre el rango de 25 a 54 años (9,4%). Y el 45% del total de desempleados tiene más de 45 años.
Si a ese sorpasso se le suma el hecho de que muchos de los desempleados de más de 50 años nunca volverán a trabajar hasta su jubilación, el escenario que se les plantea solo les deja dos salidas posibles: estirar el subsidio de desempleo para mayores de 52 años hasta su edad de jubilación ordinaria, o acogerse a una jubilación anticipada y comenzar a cobrar su pensión.
Alfonso Muñoz, funcionario de la Seguridad Social experto en jubilaciones lo deja claro en uno de sus vídeos: "Te compensa no haber solicitado la jubilación anticipada si estás cobrando el subsidio para mayores de 52 años".
La clave no es el subsido, es la cotización. El experto destaca que, si bien es cierto que el subsidio para mayores de 52 años apenas aporta 480 euros al mes sin pagas extra, una cifra que equivale al 80% del IPREM y que lleva congelada desde 2023. Pero detrás de esa cifra modesta hay algo que muy pocos tienen en cuenta: mientras se cobra esta prestación, la cotización a la Seguridad Social se calcula sobre el 125% de la base mínima de cotización.
Eso significa que, aunque el beneficiario de ese subsidio apenas note una ayuda en sus ingresos, su futura pensión sigue creciendo con una base de cotización que en 2026 ronda los 1.726 euros mensuales. "Una cantidad que nos ayudará a mantener nuestra pensión de jubilación en el futuro", explicaba Muñoz.
El precio de adelantar la jubilación. Si bien es cierto que la cuantía del subsidio de desempleo puede ser insuficiente para la subsistencia inmediata, adelantar la jubilación tiene un coste que se pagará cada mes para el resto de la vida.
Los coeficientes reductores recortan la pensión de forma permanente según los meses que se anticipe el retiro y los años que se hayan cotizado. Cuanto antes se pida la jubilación anticipada, más se nota el recorte, llegando a superar el 21% de reducción.
Muñoz lo ilustra con un ejemplo en el que, a un trabajador al que le faltan dos años para la edad ordinaria de jubilación le corresponderían 1.300 euros si se jubila con antelación, frente a 1.550 euros si aguanta cobrando el subsidio de desempleo (y cotizando) hasta la edad legal. Esto supone una diferencia de 250 euros cada mes, de por vida.
Esperar compensa. Durante esos dos años de espera hasta alcanzar la edad de jubilación ordinaria, quien mantiene el subsidio de desempleo para mayores de 52 años ingresa poco más de 11.500 euros. En cambio, quien se jubila de forma anticipada triplica sus ingresos hasta los 36.400 euros, contando pagas extra. La diferencia supera los 24.000 euros, y suena a que la jubilación anticipada gana por goleada.
Pero Muñoz matiza dividiendo esa diferencia de 24.000 euros entre los 250 euros mensuales de más que daría la pensión ordinaria. El resultado: a partir del séptimo año de jubilación, la opción de mantenerse cobrando el subsidio de desempleo y aguantar hasta los 65 años se posiciona como la elección más interesante ya que permite una mayor cuantía en la pensión durante el resto de la vida.
No hay una respuesta única para todos. Las estimaciones de Muñoz solo contemplan un horizonte de jubilación cercano (de dos años) y, a medida que se va alejando de ese horizonte, la opción de mantenerse con 480 euros al mes va siendo cada vez menos interesante.
El ejemplo que propone el funcionario demuestra que, el diseño de este subsidio no desincentiva la búsqueda de trabajo para aquellos que están más cerca de los 52 años que de los 65 años, y en cambio, aporta una salida sostenible para quienes han perdido su empleo en los últimos años de su vida laboral.

articles.title: Incroyable : Apple divise par deux le prix de sa chiffonnette de luxe
articles.text:
Parmi les annonces d’Apple, aux côtés des puces M6, des nouveaux Mac Mini et Mac Studio, une mise à jour d’un autre genre s’est glissée très discrètement dans le catalogue. Lancée à 19 dollars en 2021, la célèbre chiffonnette de la marque connaît une baisse spectaculaire de son prix en passant de 19 à 9 dollars. Profitez-en, ce sera probablement le seul produit de la marque à voir son prix baisser cette année.
Une chiffonnette de luxe deux fois moins chère
Rien ne semble changer sur la fiche technique par rapport à la version d’origine. On peut y lire :
« Fabriquée dans un matériau doux et non abrasif, la chiffonnette nettoie n’importe quel écran Apple, y compris les modèles équipés du verre nano-texturé, de manière sûre et efficace. »
La chiffonnette fonctionne ainsi sur beaucoup d’appareils de la marque, des iMac aux MacBook en passant par les iPhone. Seule ombre au tableau pour les produits sortis le même jour, à l’image du Mac Mini ou du Mac Studio, ils ne figurent pas sur la liste des appareils compatibles pour la simple raison… qu’ils ne possèdent pas d’écran.
Apple est-il devenu raisonnable ?
Initialement lancée à 25 € chez nous, la chiffonnette a beaucoup fait parler au moment de son lancement, se positionnant instantanément parmi les accessoires les plus décriés de la marque. Nous n’avons malheureusement pas réussi à le retrouver sur le site français d’Apple, mais il est bien affiché à 9 dollars sur le site américain, au lieu de 19 dollars précédemment.
À lire : Inconnus du grand public, ces 10 accessoires Apple que l’histoire a oubliés
Reste maintenant à voir s’il sera compatible avec les écrans OLED des futurs MacBook Pro, ou si une « chiffonnette Pro Max » verra le jour. Plus sérieusement, un doute subsiste sur la taille exacte du chiffon. L’entreprise n’a jamais publié les dimensions précises sur la page officielle du produit, ce qui laisse une petite possibilité pour que ce tarif plus bas s’explique par une taille réduite. Il faudra attendre les premières livraisons chez les clients pour vérifier si les dimensions de cette version ont évolué.

articles.title: Pourquoi Nvidia veut dépenser 12,9 milliards de dollars pour Hugging Face
articles.text:
Nvidia pourrait mettre la main sur l’une des principales plateformes où sont publiés et découverts des modèles, des jeux de données et des outils d’IA ouverts.
Selon The Information, la firme de Jensen Huang a accepté de racheter Hugging Face — une plateforme américaine fondée par trois Français — pour 12,9 milliards de dollars (soit environ 11 milliards d’euros). Le média cite une personne ayant connaissance de l’accord. Contactées par Reuters, les deux entreprises n’avaient toutefois pas encore commenté l’information le 27 août 2026.
L’opération doit donc encore être considérée avec prudence : elle n’a pas été annoncée officiellement et ses conditions restent inconnues. Si elle aboutit, elle figurerait parmi les plus importantes acquisitions de Nvidia en valeur.
Pourquoi Hugging Face est-il si important ?
Le prix peut surprendre. L’activité principale de Hugging Face n’est pas de commercialiser un grand modèle propriétaire comparable à ceux d’OpenAI ou d’Anthropic. Son importance vient plutôt de tout ce qu’elle rassemble.
Souvent présenté comme le « GitHub de l’IA », Hugging Face permet aux chercheurs, aux entreprises et aux développeurs de publier des modèles, des jeux de données et de petites applications. On peut y trouver aussi bien les créations de Meta, Google ou Microsoft que celles de laboratoires chinois, de chercheurs indépendants ou de parfaits inconnus.
La plateforme comptait 13 millions d’utilisateurs à la fin de 2025. En août 2026, elle hébergeait près de trois millions de modèles publics, un million de jeux de données et plus de 1,4 million d’applications de démonstration, selon les chiffres publiés par Hugging Face. Tous ne sont pas nécessairement « open source » au sens strict : certaines entreprises rendent les paramètres de leurs modèles accessibles tout en imposant des restrictions sur leur utilisation.
La plupart de ces dépôts restent presque invisibles. Hugging Face estime que 85,6 % des modèles ont été téléchargés moins de 200 fois, tandis que 1,5 % des dépôts concentrent 99,2 % des téléchargements. Mais cette immense bibliothèque est devenue une porte d’entrée incontournable pour découvrir, tester et déployer de nouvelles IA.
C’est cette position centrale que Nvidia serait prêt à payer très cher. D’après The Information, Hugging Face ne générerait qu’environ 150 millions de dollars de revenus annualisés. Le prix évoqué correspondrait donc à 86 fois ce montant et presque au triple de la valorisation de 4,5 milliards de dollars obtenue lors de sa dernière levée de fonds en 2023.
Même un agent d’OpenAI est allé chercher des réponses chez Hugging Face
Un incident survenu en juillet 2026 a montré, de manière beaucoup moins rassurante, à quel point Hugging Face était devenu central. La firme a alors détecté et neutralisé une intrusion dans son infrastructure de production. Dans la foulée, OpenAI a attribué l’incident à ses propres modèles : GPT-5.6 Sol et un modèle pre-release encore plus performant, tous deux configurés avec des refus cyber réduits pour les besoins d’une évaluation interne.
Ces modèles sont parvenus à sortir de leur environnement isolé, puis à compromettre une partie des systèmes de Hugging Face pour récupérer les solutions d’un benchmark de cybersécurité baptisé ExploitGym. OpenAI a reconnu un « incident cyber sans précédent », tandis que Hugging Face a publié une chronologie technique détaillée.
L’épisode n’a, au premier abord, aucun lien direct avec le projet de rachat. Il illustre toutefois la valeur stratégique de la plateforme : lorsqu’un agent cherche un modèle, un jeu de données ou même les réponses à une évaluation, Hugging Face fait partie des premiers endroits où il peut aller.
Quelques jours après l’incident, Nvidia et Hugging Face ont d’ailleurs participé au lancement de l’Open Secure AI Alliance, qui cite notamment cette attaque pour justifier le développement de nouveaux outils de sécurité ouverts. Un rachat permettrait à Nvidia d’aller beaucoup plus loin, en prenant directement le contrôle de l’une des principales infrastructures que ces outils doivent protéger.
D’autant que les deux entreprises se connaissaient déjà très bien : Nvidia avait participé à la levée de fonds de la startup en 2023, aux côtés notamment de Google, Amazon, Intel, AMD, Salesforce et IBM.
Elles ont depuis multiplié les passerelles. Dès 2023, elles annonçaient l’intégration de DGX Cloud, le service de calcul de Nvidia, directement dans Hugging Face. Un développeur peut ainsi choisir un modèle sur la plateforme, puis louer les infrastructures nécessaires pour l’entraîner ou l’adapter.
En 2025, les deux entreprises ont aussi lancé un service permettant de réserver des grappes de puces Nvidia depuis Hugging Face. En rachetant la plateforme, Nvidia contrôlerait donc la vitrine où de nombreux développeurs choisissent leurs modèles et la puissance de calcul nécessaire pour les utiliser.
Hugging Face pourrait-il encore rester neutre ?
C’est notamment là que le rachat pourrait susciter des questions. Hugging Face ne travaille pas seulement avec Nvidia : ses outils permettent aussi d’exécuter des modèles sur des puces AMD, des processeurs Intel ou les infrastructures de plusieurs fournisseurs de cloud. En 2024, la plateforme expliquait encore collaborer avec Nvidia, AMD et Intel.
Cette indépendance semblait pourtant lui tenir à cœur. Selon le Financial Times, Hugging Face aurait refusé en 2025 un investissement de 500 millions de dollars de Nvidia, qui l’aurait valorisée 7 milliards, par crainte de laisser un acteur aussi puissant peser sur ses décisions.
Nvidia pourrait évidemment maintenir la plateforme ouverte à tous. Il lui serait toutefois facile de mieux intégrer ses propres services ou de les mettre davantage en avant. En clair, le groupe ne rachèterait donc pas seulement une startup fondée par trois Français, mais un lieu central de l’IA ouverte, utilisé par ses clients comme par ceux de ses concurrents

articles.title: US Disrupts Chinese Hacking Platform Used in Military and Critical Infrastructure Attacks
articles.text:
The US government announced on Wednesday that it has disrupted a hacking platform and botnet used by Chinese threat actors in attacks aimed at military and critical infrastructure systems.
According to the Justice Department, the disruption efforts targeted a state-sponsored group called QTFY, which has been operating from a company called Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology.
QTFY has offered its hacking services to the Chinese government and others, enabling attacks against many critical systems in the United States since its establishment in 2018.
Disruption of QTFY hacking platform
The US government has targeted two hacking services offered by QTFY: the scanning and exploitation platform QScan, and the obfuscation network QTRouter.
QScan is designed to scan the internet for vulnerable IoT devices and ensnare them in the QTRouter botnet, enabling threat actors to abuse the compromised devices to conceal their malicious activities and evade detection.
US authorities identified and seized domains used by QScan and QTRouter.
“Because the seized domains were hard-coded into both the QScan and QTRouter malware and used for essential tasks such as communication and authentication, the court-authorized seizures made QScan and QTRouter inoperable,” explained the Justice Department.
QTFY attacks and exploitation
A technical cybersecurity advisory published on Wednesday by the FBI reveals that QTFY has been developing malicious tools, trading malware and exploits, and maintaining botnets to carry out its attacks.
Targeted sectors include the defense industrial base, local government, telecoms, and higher education.
The agency said some of the group’s attempts to hack sensitive networks were unsuccessful, including attacks aimed at the Department of Energy, election systems, the Department of Health and Human Services, the US Senate, a children’s hospital, a semiconductor company, and a power company.
Other attacks appear to have been successful at least to some extent, including against NASA, the Justice Department, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy, state governments, a major retailer, a telecoms company, defense contractors, universities, and financial institutions.
The hackers have been observed exploiting vulnerabilities in products from BeyondTrust, CrushFTP, Ivanti, Check Point, Atlassian, Kentico, F5, Microsoft, Citrix, Fortinet, and Pulse Secure.
“QTFY actors are active in the exploit development community, freelance PRC [People’s Republic of China] hacker networks, and PRC malicious cyber contracting and subcontracting marketplaces,” the FBI noted. “QTFY participates in the offensive end of network attack and defense events against Chinese critical infrastructure.”
The FBI also pointed out that the company behind QTFY has had business relationships with various entities connected to the Salt Typhoon cyberespionage group, the i-Soon cyber intrusion firm, and several others.
